385YE Autumn Equinox Imperial elections.d: National elections returned senators for ten territories, including Solomon for Casinea, Hengest Dun for Hahnmark and two League seats for Spiral and Tassato. The Senate appointed six generals, among them the generals of the Bounders, Eastern Sky and Wolves of War, plus an Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves. The Synod elected Sabella of the Silent Tide as Cardinal of Loyalty and Zadkiel de Coeurdefer as Cardinal of Pride. The Military Council filled posts including Quartermaster General and Imperial Warcaster. The Conclave chose two grandmasters, and the Bourse awarded seats such as the Fortress of Salt (451 thrones) and Castellan of Spiral Castle (603 votes).

n.Dawn: Dawn's territory of Semmerholm returned Amicia of the Semmerlak as its senator.
n.Highguard: Highguard's territory of Casinea elected Solomon as its senator.
n.Navarr: Navarr's territory of Therunin returned Travid Longest Path as its senator.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast's territory of Kahraman elected Delara i Fijadoz i Guerra as its senator.
n.The League: The League filled two Senate seats, with Genoveva Barossa d'Apulian elected for Spiral and Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato for Tassato.
n.The Marches: The Marches' territory of Upwold elected Johnny Tailor as its senator.
n.Urizen: Urizen's territory of Morrow returned Laelius Archsky as its senator.
n.Varushka: Varushka's territory of Volodmartz elected Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen as its senator.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's territory of Hahnmark returned Hengest Dun as its senator.

t.Casinea: Solomon was elected Senator for Casinea.
t.Hahnmark: Hengest Dun was elected Senator for Hahnmark.
t.Kahraman: Delara i Fijadoz i Guerra was elected Senator for Kahraman.

t.Semmerholm: Amicia of the Semmerlak was elected Senator for Semmerholm.

385YE Autumn Equinox Senate sessions.d: The treasury stood at 602 thrones and 4 crowns. Administrative motions ruled the Vendarri barbarians under the 379YE war on the orcs of the Barrens, and left the Montanians as barbarians. The Senate declared war on the Grendel, funded military resupply in Karsk (400 thrones) and the Wintermark army (175 thrones), raised a third Imperial Orc army in Skarsind and gave the Quartermaster General a 300-throne stipend. New titles included the Citizens' Voice, the Benefactor of Regalia and the National Strategos. Commissions and announcements created works in Volodmartz, Zenith, Holberg, Tassato, Kahraman, Miaren, Mitwold, Kallavesa, Reikos, Temeschwar, the Mournwold, Hahnmark and Ossium. Thalia of Netherwatch and Xanthius were elected to Imperial titles.

n.Dawn: Dawnish senators drove several motions, with Semmerholm proposing the war on the Grendel, Astolat securing a 300-throne stipend for the Quartermaster General and Weirwater commissioning an appraisal of the damaged Spider's Dream tollbridge.
n.Druj: The Senate confirmed that the Winter 379YE declaration of war on the orcs of the Barrens includes the Vendarri, and its failure to extend the peace treaty left the Montanians active in the Barrens classed as barbarians.
n.Grendel: The Senate declared war on the Grendel, who are now considered barbarians under Imperial law.
n.Highguard: Highborn senators created the Benefactor of Regalia, appointed by their unanimous decision, and the national Strategos titles, and commissioned the Greenwatch ministry in Reikos to aid those fighting the vallorn; a proposed great work in Holberg towards Highguard's debt to the League was withdrawn.
n.Imperial Orcs: A third Imperial Orc army, the Autumn Hammers, began raising in Skarsind from the Ethengraw sept.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are not named; the page's only link is Bregasland, where the Senate sent magistrates to root out traitorous households.
n.Navarr: The Senate built Stones from Blood, a mana ministry in Miaren for the Navarr vates council, while Navarri senators proposed the Throne election and the roads appraisal.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gained the Red Depths, a self-funded mithril national bourse seat in Kahraman, and 25 thrones for the Kahraman roads and Kamkrag forts project, while Madruga's senator created the Citizens' Voice.
n.The League: The League gained the Legacy in Spiral as a national bourse seat, the Lakesedge Highway, Holberg's Melodious Cascade and the Gates of Holmauer Park in Holberg, the Five Cities Military Academy in Tassato and the School of Hard Knocks in Temeschwar.
n.The Marches: Marcher senators dredged the Westmere to create a mithril ministry in Meade, and though the Townsend Treasury motion failed it was later announced as a sinecure in Sarcombe; Bambrick's Lament was withdrawn.
n.Urizen: Urizen repaired the Tower of the Fall in Zenith, secured 35 thrones a season for mana to shroud its remaining spires in Spiral, and saw Thalia of Netherwatch and Xanthius elected Ambassador to the Sarcophan Delves and Guildmaster of the Artisans.
n.Varushka: Varushka gained the Deep Place and the Triosk Metal Exchange in Volodmartz and Kurstrozi's Lumbermill in Ossium, plus 400 thrones for military resupply via Karsk's senator; a proposal to drown the condemned in the Semmerlak was withdrawn.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark received 175 thrones towards its half-levied army, the Bright-Threads Brass Works in Hahnmark and an ilium ministry in Fisk, Kallavesa, and Sermersuaq's senator created the Writ of Consecration.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat's senator proposed the Quartermaster General's stipend and seconded the Five Cities Military Academy.
t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: Bastion's senator seconded the war on the Grendel and proposed a withdrawn great work in Holberg.
t.Bregasland: Magistrates were sent in force to root out traitorous households, imposing a one-rank penalty on every personal resource in Bregasland until the Winter Solstice.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: Casinea's senator proposed the National Strategos titles and seconded the Benefactor of Regalia; the Greenwatch was proposed for Casinea but recorded as built in Reikos.
t.Hahnmark: The Bright-Threads Brass Works orichalcum sinecure was built in Hahnmark, and its senator received 175 thrones for the Wintermark army.
t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Hercynia's senator proposed the Throne election and seconded the Greenwatch.
t.Holberg: Holberg gained the Lakesedge Highway sinecure through Rebeshof, Holberg's Melodious Cascade and the Gates of Holmauer Park great work; a motion to make Semmerlak drowning its default execution was withdrawn.
t.Kahraman: The Red Depths mithril bourse seat was created in Kahraman, and 25 thrones went to its roads and Kamkrag forts project.
t.Kallavesa: Dredging the Westmere created an ilium ministry in Fisk held by the Mediator of Fisk.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: Karov's senator proposed the withdrawn Semmerlak drowning motion and seconded the Dean of the Academy amendment.
t.Karsk: Karsk's senator received 400 thrones for military resupply.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga's senator proposed the Citizens' Voice and seconded the Spider's Dream appraisal.
t.Miaren: The Stones from Blood mana ministry for the Navarr vates council was built in Miaren.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Miekarova's senator proposed the Sarcophan Delves ambassador election and seconded the Deep Place.
t.Mitwold: Dredging the Westmere at Meade March created a mithril ministry in Meade held by the Alder of Meade.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: Morrow's senator proposed the failed Arcane Architect amendment and seconded the Dean election.
t.Mournwold: After the Senate motion failed, the Townsend Treasury money sinecure in Sarcombe was created by announcement.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: Necropolis's senator proposed the Benefactor of Regalia and seconded the Strategos titles.
t.Ossium: Kurstrozi's Lumbermill great work was commissioned in Drownbark to increase the prosperity of Ossium's forests.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: Redoubt's senator proposed the Dean of the Academy amendment and seconded the Spiral mana motion.
t.Reikos: The Greenwatch ministry, supporting those who fight the vallorn, was constructed in Reikos.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos's senator seconded the withdrawn drowning motion and proposed the Dean election.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: Segura's senator proposed the Red Depths and seconded the Lakesedge Highway.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm's senator proposed the war on the Grendel, and the territory was named in the withdrawn drowning motion.
t.Sermersuaq: Mentioned in passing: Sermersuaq's senator proposed the Writ of Consecration and seconded the Wintermark army funding.
t.Skarsind: The Autumn Hammers, a third Imperial Orc army, began raising in Skarsind from the Ethengraw sept.
t.Spiral: The Legacy was made a League bourse seat, and 35 thrones a season will buy mana to cast Vale of Shadows over the remaining Urizeni spires.
t.Tassato: The Five Cities Military Academy folly was constructed in Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: The School of Hard Knocks sinecure was built in Temeschwar, creating the Maestro of Wolves.
t.The Barrens: The Vendarri were ruled barbarians under the existing war on the orcs of the Barrens, and the Montanians active there remain barbarians.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: Therunin's senator proposed the roads appraisal and seconded the Legacy allocation.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: Upwold's senator seconded the Bregasland investigation and proposed the withdrawn Bambrick's Lament.
t.Volodmartz: The Deep Place mine workings in Brez and the Triosk Metal Exchange were both built as ministries in Volodmartz.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater's senator proposed the Spider's Dream appraisal, and the territory was named in the withdrawn drowning motion.
t.Zenith: The Tower of the Fall in Occursion was rebuilt as a mana sinecure joining the Proffered Hand network.

r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: The Bright-Threads Brass Works, an orichalcum sinecure, was built in Valasmark.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer gained Holberg's Melodious Cascade and the Gates of Holmauer Park, and the Lakesedge Highway begins at the Holmauer Gate.

385YE Autumn Equinox Synod judgements.d: Clarice Novarion's change of doctrine was upheld with a greater majority (3013–159). The Assembly of Nine declined to veto the Throne's election. Aurum's mandate means that any army sent against the Urizeni rebels in Spiral before Autumn 386YE will spread rebellion across Urizen. Herminius's mandate sundered the sword scholars from Sulemaine, shattering the Temple of the Four Winds and weakening Urizen congregations. Navarr, backed by the Eyes of Loyalty, was urged to help the Great Forest Orcs take the Heart of Peytaht. Wintermark and Navarr committed resources to the sacred city in Bastion. The Marches welcomed the Mournwold Orcs, and the Imperial Orcs took the name Unshackled. Jared of the Suns of Couros was revoked as Lepidean Librarian.

n.Dawn: Dawn's assembly crowned its yearly champions, celebrated the return of the Rod of the Sun and set out rules for the girding of Black Knights. It urged vigilance against the Druj and restraint towards the Montanians of the Barrens, and opened Dawnish homes to the Free Folk, while Ser Dindrane's Laroc mandate failed.
n.Druj: The Vigilance assembly advocated cursing the Druj heartland of Sanath. A Highborn mandate set the Valiant Pegasus to limit casualties and open talks with orc septs oppressed by the Druj in the Salt Flats.
n.Grendel: With the Grendel treaty ended, the Freeborn assembly vowed to reclaim Feroz, called for raids on enemy shipping in the Bay of Catazar and urged citizens to root out Grendel spies. Urizen priests warned the Spiral rebels that the Grendel were coming.
n.Highguard: The Highborn invited the Free Folk to settle in Highguard, affirmed that lineage is a matter of the body rather than the spirit, and offered Peerless Kinship to the Imperial Orcs, who accepted it. Their priests also rallied veterans under the Thundering Tide to defend Bastion from the Cold Sun, and Hazelelponi replaced the revoked Jared as Lepidean Librarian.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orc assembly claimed the name Unshackled for their nation, accepted Highguard's Peerless Kinship and sent supplies to the Rahvin in Bitter Strand. The Synod's new Doctrine of Enlightenment declares orcs and humans equal in Virtue.
n.Jotun: A Freeborn mandate ensures visiting Jotun ghodi are escorted safely to raise a monument at their burial mound in Kahraman. The General Assembly urged those fighting the Jotun to respect their dead and leave their sacred sites undesecrated.
n.Navarr: A Navarr mandate, supported by the Eyes of Loyalty, lets Navarr armies help the Great Forest Orcs claim the Heart of Peytaht. Another commits every affected Navarr territory to donate 12 wains of white granite and 24 crowns each season for a year towards the sacred city in Bastion.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn assembly vowed to reclaim Feroz, urged raids on enemy shipping and vigilance against Grendel spies, and backed the corsairs' wish for their own leader. It also sent an honour guard to escort the Jotun at Kahraman and called on corsairs to rescue escaping slaves from Marlien.
n.The League: League priests urged sending mana from Lorenzo's Legacies to help the Urizeni spires of Spiral, and called for dialogue with Urizen and the Apulian Orcs rather than warfare. League bishops also offered to show Apulian questioners how to use the Synod's powers.
n.The Marches: The Marcher assembly's mandate declared the former Jotun thrall orcs to be Marchers. It also backed inquisitors hunting supporters of the Fisher rebellion in Bregasland, declared Sadogua a friend to Marcher wizards and warned miners about the Wanderer, while a call to boycott food sales to Urizen failed.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Gisli is praised for raising money to feed the Thule, and Varushkan wardens are asked to protect the caravans of the Thule warlock Orathator of the Hourglass.
n.Urizen: Aurum's mandate threatens nationwide Urizeni rebellion if the Empire sends an army against the rebels in Spiral, though Callista's call to spread the uprising failed. Herminius's mandate shattered the Temple of the Four Winds and cost every Urizen congregation two votes and one liao. The assembly also urged raising a second army and thanked Varushka for helping build the Gardens of Pallas in Zenith.
n.Varushka: Varushkan priests urged fleet owners to prepare for war and asked wardens to strengthen the wards around Tolvoli against the dubik. They also invited Skywise Gralka to the Palace of Orieb, called for pride in the Northern Eagle and were thanked by Urizen for their wayleave gift.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's assembly added Atte Arrowtongue and Helgunn Chargebringer to the Chronicle of Heroism, called for an artisan academy and sought news of the banner Foeslayer. Its mandate commits each affected territory to 4 wains of white granite and 8 crowns a season for a year towards the sacred city in Bastion.

t.Bastion: Wintermark and Navarr mandates direct white granite and money to the sacred city being built here, and the Virtue Fund made a partial contribution. Highborn priests also urged its defence against the Cold Sun's forces gathering there and backed an inspirational monument at Berechiah's basilica.
t.Bregasland: The Marcher assembly backed the Senator for Bregasland in sending inquisitors to find those who supported the Mathilda Fisher rebellion. It asked Bregas priests to offer clemency pleas for the virtuous.
t.Feroz: The Freeborn assembly declared Feroz an integral part of the Brass Coast and vowed to reclaim it. Its earlier mandate abandoning the territory makes further opportunities unlikely.
t.Hahnmark: Wintermark's priests urged the courageous to garrison the Beacons of Wintermark, which stand in Hahnmark, against the Cold Sun.
t.Kahraman: A Freeborn mandate provides an honour guard escorting Jotun ghodi to raise a monument at the burial mound here, which prevents their capture. Helgunn Chargebringer, who fell in Kahraman, was added to the Chronicle of Heroism.
t.Kallavesa: Wintermark's priests called for the Beacons of Wintermark, which stand in Kallavesa, to be garrisoned against the Cold Sun. The lost banner Foeslayer was said to have been interred in the Kallavesi swamps.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Marcher assembly exalted Jonathan Piper, who had earlier warned the people of Mitwold about heralds of Siakha.
t.Necropolis: The Highborn assembly praised the Imperial Orcs' campaign to reclaim items of worth in the Necropolis. Wintermark called for Britta's memorial here to be linked as a place of pilgrimage with her pool in the Sovevann.
t.Ossium: The Varushkan assembly invited Skywise Gralka and the Sunstorm sept to seek secrets at the Palace of Orieb in Ossium.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the League's mana offer may help the spires of Spiral stay connected to their fellows in Zenith and Redoubt.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Vigilance assembly advocated cursing Sanath while the Citadel Guard are present. A Highborn mandate commits the Valiant Pegasus to minimise casualties and open communication with the orc septs while fighting here.
t.Sermersuaq: Atte Arrowtongue was honoured partly for working to lift up Sermersuaq. Two assemblies warned that three Blood-on-the-Snow cultist leaders remain at large after its liberation.
t.Spiral: Spiral dominated the Synod's business. Aurum's mandate means any army sent against its Urizeni rebels before Autumn 386YE will spread rebellion across Urizen. League and Urizen priests pressed for reckoning and dialogue, and Urizen resumed using the mithril block to protect the spires.
t.The Barrens: Several assemblies debated whether the Empire came to the Barrens as liberators or conquerors, urging restraint towards the Montanians and education in the Way. Mandates were also passed supporting the Great Forest Orcs and the Rahvin.
t.The Semmerlak: A statement defending the drowning of criminals in the Semmerlak to satisfy Dho'uala failed narrowly and was withdrawn.
t.Zenith: Urizen priests noted that Zenith is being rebuilt and thanked Varushka for the wayleave used to build the Gardens of Pallas here. A Marcher inquisition over a curse on Zenith was withdrawn.

r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Imperial Orc priests deliver food and supplies to the Rahvin here. This makes the sept well disposed towards the Imperial Orcs and willing to negotiate with them on the Empire's behalf.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: Any Navarr army in the Barrens that explicitly attacks the Heart of Peytaht in support of the Great Forest Orcs can help them conquer it. The orcs would then claim the region without needing the Senate to concede it.

385YE Autumn Equinox interlude.d: Dawnish and Navarri units could fight the heralds of Cold Sun. Freeborn and League units could guard Kahraman's caravans at Senate expense. Highborn and Varushkan units could arm and train the Dreamers of the Dark Forest in Echofell. Freeborn corsairs and Highborn fleets could help ships slip through the Asavean blockade of Sumaah ports. Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths added ingots to every Imperial mine. Dawnish magicians infused their four territories with Summer magic. Tharim began feasting on Brass Coast and Dawnish resources in return for military support. Dho'uala's harassment of Semmerlak fleets eased. The Guerdon stood at 350 thrones, shared among five armies.

n.Dawn: Dawnish units could defend their people against Cold Sun, and all four Dawnish territories were infused with Summer magic. Dawnish mana sites and farms paid a tithe to Tharim in return for support for an army in the Barrens, while Dawnish fleets were temporarily freed from Dho'uala's penalty.
n.Druj: The Dreamers sept were being armed and trained to drive the remaining Druj out of Echofell's forest depths. Tharim's knights would also support a Dawnish army fighting in the Barrens.
n.Grendel: Grendel merchants traded enthusiastically with Highborn businesses in Necropolis under the Wildfyre mandate. Grendel's continued hold on Feroz kept the Atalaya Harbour discount in place for Madruga.
n.Highguard: Highguard faced reduced mana from the hunt for the Whisper Gallery and a production penalty on every business to fund Free Folk tutelage. Against this, its congregations gained liao, votes and income from the Birthplace of the Way, and its units and fleets could train the Dreamers or thwart the blockade.
n.Navarr: With the Navarri assembly's statement reaching their priests in time, Navarri military units could take up the fight against the heralds of Cold Sun.
n.The Brass Coast: Tharim's black frost drained a crystal from every Freeborn mana site and three drams of true vervain from every herb garden, in return for supporting the Fire of the South. Freeborn units could guard Kahraman's caravans, and corsairs could help thwart the Asavean blockade.
n.The League: League units could take paid work guarding Kahraman's caravans, and League congregations preaching Ambition gained liao and Synod votes. League businesses were also cheaper to upgrade during a grand competition.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: no new rituals were added to Urizen lore during the Summer Solstice.
n.Varushka: Varushkan units could help arm and train the Dreamers in Echofell, and Varushkan fleets were temporarily freed from Dho'uala's harassment. The Deadwood Knight's curse did not fall on Karov.

t.Astolat: Astolat was infused with Summer magic by Dawnish magicians aided by Meraud, likely drawing heralds of that realm to its people.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: the Madruga fleet upgrade discount would last only as long as the Freeborn did not control Feroz.
t.Holberg: Holberg's fleets were freed, for this season at least, from the one-rank production penalty caused by Dho'uala's harassment on the Semmerlak.
t.Kahraman: The Senate paid for guards and mercenaries to give Kahraman's people short-term protection from raiders, smugglers, bandits and accidents, using Freeborn and League units.
t.Karov: Although the Deadwood Knight was defeated, for some reason their curse did not fall on Karov.
t.Madruga: While the Atalaya Harbour remained, fleets in Madruga cost one less wain of weirwood to upgrade.
t.Necropolis: Visiting Grendel traders dealt with Highborn businesses in Necropolis, giving each business an extra 2 crowns a season.
t.Ossium: Training the Dreamers sept to drive out the remaining Druj could, with Senate approval, lift Ossium's under-threat quality.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm was infused with Summer magic, likely encouraging heralds of that realm to visit.
t.The Barrens: The Barrens were infused with Summer magic alongside Dawn's other territories. Tharim pledged steel-bound support to a Dawnish army fighting there.
t.The Semmerlak: Dho'uala's harassment of Dawnish, Varushkan and Holberg fleets on the Semmerlak eased this season. However, the Custodian of Ivarsgard Docks and the Harbourmaster of the Semmerlak faced higher prices, and the Harbourmaster lost access to ilium.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater was infused with Summer magic, and every herb garden there would yield an extra dose of bladeroot from the defeated Deadwood Knight's boon.

r.Ossium/Echofell: The Dreamers of the Dark Forest sept in Echofell were being given weapons, armour and training by Highborn and Varushkan units so they could drive the remaining Druj from the forest.

385YE Autumn Equinox winds of fortune.d: This index introduced eighteen winds of fortune. Among them were eternal plenipotentiary responses, two Senate appraisals on raiding and on Spiral, and new mineral wealth exposed at Redgate Pass. Others covered magicians' unease over Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths and the murderous Cold Sun heralds, the angry orc septs of the newly Dawnish Barrens, the Sulemaine debate among the sword scholars, three Marcher dilemmas, the Apulian orcs, the League's city competition, Highguard's cities, Jotun envoys and foreign affairs. Shorter notes reported the completed expansion of the Hacynian library and powerful rituals cast. A trade summary followed, with Axos hostile over the Mountains of the Moon. Most conjunction tables record successes, though Fort Braydon collapsed and several missions suffered losses.

n.Dawn: With the Barrens conquered and assigned to Dawn, the nation celebrates while its National Assembly pursues working with the angry orc septs rather than settling the land. The Regents of Summer reportedly ensured no Dawnish citizen fell to the soldiers of Day.
n.Druj: The Druj lost the Barrens for good and suffered defeats at Oakenclough, the Silent Glade, Thicket of Thorns and Broken Clearing, and Varag Soulflayer was slain. Highborn voices also urged a liberating approach on the road to Leen in the Salt Flats.
n.Grendel: Orcs who once followed former Salt Lord Kaliact are joining the League as Apulians, Grendel agents have been uncovered in the League, and war with the Grendel is widely expected. The port of Oran remains closed to Imperial fleets.
n.Highguard: The Highborn helped Dawn make contact with the Barrens septs and supported the Hacynian vallorn research. The Cities and the City covers spies, malevolent heralds and dark powers in Bastion and Necropolis.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: listed among the interested parties for the When Spring Comes and The Cities and the City winds.
n.Jotun: After Brass Coast respect at Fort Braydon and Wintermark's honourable fighting in Tromsa, a young ghodi and a northern envoy came seeking talks, the latter bearing a request. Elsewhere Jotun forces were slain in Torres, Enterio and Greenwall, Magnus Ironarm and Blade Quencher died, and Jarl Haakon retreated from the Mournwold.
n.Navarr: The expansion of the Great Library at Hacynian is complete, and vallorn research is expected by the Summer Solstice 386YE if invading forces in Northpines do not strike. Navarr scholars were invited to take part, and the Pool of Silver Clouds in Goldglades was protected at heavy cost.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn face the eternal Tharim's raids on mana sites and herb gardens, new mineral opportunities at Redgate Pass in Kahraman, and a Jotun ghodi drawn by their respect at Fort Braydon, which has since collapsed. Their assembly also lifted the Asavean blockade of Zemeh.
n.The League: The League grapples with an appraisal on Urizen loyalty in Spiral, a contested first Senate election for Spiral, and its city competition, now turning towards education. It also faces Grendel agents uncovered in Sarvos and the Sand Fishers' logging of Misericorde.
n.The Marches: Marchers face three dilemmas: Day and Maelstrom heralds in Mitwold, the risk of violence in the Dour Fens of Bregasland, and the question of the Mournwold Orcs coming to a head. Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths has also raised serious issues in the nation, and Marcher fleets enjoy a bonus trading at Caitun.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Thule warlocks keen to speak with experts on the vallorn are among the visitors expected at Anvil.
n.Urizen: The Urizen of Spiral simmer in open rebellion, a matter the Spiral appraisal tries to untangle. The Urizen Assembly's praise of Sulemaine and a plan to consecrate her tomb have reignited debate over the sword scholars' inspiration.
n.Varushka: The last of the Varushkan vyig was killed at Butterfly Holt in Srodkoja. Varushka is also tagged in The Cities and the City, and the Guardian of the Maze of Zoria in the winds of magic.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's armies led the charge deep into Tromsa, and their honourable conduct has prompted the Jotun to respond in kind and send an envoy to the generals. A Jotun ghodi also hopes to discuss ancestors with the Winterfolk.

t.Astolat: Astolat is expected to celebrate the Barrens' assignment to Dawn, and sword scholars have been invited to teach at Laroc. The Harps of Astolat were protected at the Gardens of House Cadence, though with Imperial losses.
t.Bastion: Bastion is one of four cities whose challenges, including spies and malevolent heralds, are explored in The Cities and the City.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named directly on this page.
t.Bregasland: The legacy of the Fishers lingers in Bregasland, and the Dour Fens risk erupting into violence at any moment. Bushel Sykes was murdered at the Ottery Fishing Docks, and Dripping Echoes of the Fen was cast in the Grey Fens.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: information recovered from Brocéliande is aiding the vallorn research at Hacynian.
t.Feroz: The Archmage of Spring used a conjunction to meet emissaries of Siakha at Azcara's Field; the outcome is known only to them.
t.Hercynia: The expansion of the Great Library at Hacynian is complete, but the invading forces in Northpines threaten the research timetable.
t.Holberg: Sword scholars have been invited to teach in Holberg, and Prince Bishop Jonah von Holberg's statement on scholarship has spurred League interest in education. Meanwhile the Sand Fishers have begun logging Misericorde in earnest.
t.Kahraman: The blocking of Redgate Pass sealed Serra Damata from Jotun territory and exposed mineral wealth the Empire may develop if it can afford to. Fort Braydon, left unaided, collapsed after the Summer Solstice, and Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae was cast in Serra Briante.
t.Kallavesa: The Raven Seer's band protected the Aviary of Ishal at Maiko's Copse, rescuing Maiko and slaying all the heralds.
t.Karov: Mentioned in passing: the Deadwood Knight was defeated in woods on Weirwater's border with Karov.
t.Madruga: The Tassatan vyig was ended at Renewal Grove and the documents secured, and Jotun raiders in Torres were all killed. In the Great Grasses an individual was recovered, but scholars facing the blight and the defenders of the Aldea di Tutamen estate were forced to retreat.
t.Miaren: The Pool of Silver Clouds at Verdant Grove was protected successfully, though at the cost of many Imperial lives.
t.Miekarova: The last of the Varushkan vyig was killed at Butterfly Holt.
t.Mitwold: Attacks by Day heralds in Mitwold were complicated by savage Maelstrom heralds, with an unexpected outcome. Sally Thresher of House Talbot dealt with heralds on the Long Road.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Mentioned in passing: Axos remains furious at Imperial involvement in the failure of its joint venture with the Grendel into the Mountains of the Moon.
t.Mournwold: The question of the Mournwold Orcs is coming to a head with far-reaching implications. Jarl Haakon and a small entourage escaped and retreated from the territory.
t.Necropolis: Necropolis is one of four cities whose dangers and opportunities, such as worries about dark powers, are explored in The Cities and the City.
t.Ossium: Druj and heralds were killed at Broken Clearing in Drownbark Forest with many casualties. Dripping Echoes of the Fen was cast in Drownbark Forest, and Forge the Wooden Fastness in Echofell.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Otkodov is listed among the Empire's influential neighbours, and its Ambassador is flagged in Ten Travellers Tales.
t.Reinos: The General of the Red Wind Corsairs' band killed the Jotun at Beatriz's Field and recovered the Overflowing Platter.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: On the road to Leen, the Highborn urge their fellow nations to remember they come as liberators, not conquerors.
t.Sarangrave: The Druj were defeated at the Thicket of Thorns, allowing Decius Frostspire to escape.
t.Sarvos: Grendel agents have been uncovered in the League, and events in Sarvos are among those covered in The Cities and the City.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Semmerholm is named among the Dawnish territories expected to celebrate and to be looked to for national improvement.
t.Skallahn: Blade Quencher's Hall was severed from the Autumn realm and Blade Quencher killed. Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard's Jotun were slain at Paegga's Rest, but the shield of Blerung the Bright Lantern remains in Jotun hands.
t.Spiral: Spiral's Urizen simmer in open rebellion, the subject of a Senate appraisal. Human and Apulian orc candidates contest the territory's first League Senate seat, while questions of virtue and religion remain unsettled.
t.Tassato: Magnus Ironarm died along with his Jotun at Duarte's Repose in Enterio.
t.Temeschwar: The last of the Temeschwari vyig were killed in the Broken Wilds.
t.The Barrens: Newly conquered and assigned to Dawn, the Barrens are home to orc septs angered by the decision, whom Dawn hopes to appease rather than displace. The Druj were broken at Oakenclough and defeated at the Silent Glade, Varag Soulflayer was slain, and the Shrine of Hope was consecrated to Ambition.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: the Senator for Therunin led the conjunction that defeated the Druj at the Silent Glade in the Barrens.
t.Tromsa: Wintermark's armies have taken the war deep into Tromsa, and the Jotun there have begun fighting with matching honour and sent an envoy to the generals.
t.Upwold: Benson's Orchard in Tower March, the orchard of Benson the Bellringer, was consecrated to Vigilance.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater is expected to celebrate Dawn's victory. Areloe Larmallevés investigated events at Surlac, and the Champion of Dawn defeated the Deadwood Knight near the Karov border.
t.Zenith: Dripping Echoes of the Fen was cast in Proceris.

r.Astolat/Winterbourne: The Harps of Astolat at the Gardens of House Cadence were eventually protected, though with Imperial losses.
r.Bregasland/Grey Fens: Dripping Echoes of the Fen was cast in the Grey Fens.
r.Bregasland/Ottermire: An attempted meeting with Bushel Sykes at the Ottery Fishing Docks ended with Sykes murdered.
r.Feroz/Cazar Straits: The Archmage of Spring met emissaries of Siakha at Azcara's Field, with results known only to them.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: Invading forces in Northpines threaten the Great Library at Hacynian and the vallorn research timetable.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers have begun logging the Misericorde woodlands in earnest.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae was cast in Serra Briante.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The passes into Serra Damata from Jotun territory were blocked at Redgate Pass, exposing mineral wealth the Empire might develop.
r.Kallavesa/Skymark: The Aviary of Ishal at Maiko's Copse was protected, Maiko rescued and all the heralds slain.
r.Madruga/Calvos Sound: The Tassatan vyig was ended at Renewal Grove and its documents secured.
r.Madruga/Torres: The Jotun at Fondre's Rest were stopped and all killed.
r.Miaren/Goldglades: The Pool of Silver Clouds at Verdant Grove was protected, with many Imperial losses.
r.Miekarova/Srodkoja: The last of the Varushkan vyig was killed at Butterfly Holt.
r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: Sally Thresher of House Talbot confronted heralds on the Long Road, with the outcome known only to her.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Jarl Haakon was confronted at Maggie's Croft but escaped with a small entourage and retreated from the Mournwold.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Druj and heralds were killed at Broken Clearing with many casualties, and Dripping Echoes of the Fen was cast here.
r.Ossium/Echofell: Forge the Wooden Fastness was cast in Echofell.
r.Reinos/Bastasor: The Jotun at Beatriz's Field were killed and the Overflowing Platter recovered.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Druj were defeated at the Thicket of Thorns and Decius Frostspire escaped.
r.Skallahn/Greenwall: Jarl Asbjørn Dalgaard's Jotun were all slain at Paegga's Rest.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: An attempt to recover the shield of Blerung the Bright Lantern at Kevan's Holt failed, leaving it in Jotun hands.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Many orcs in Apulus are hedging their bets about joining the League, and the senatorial seat once styled Apulus is now contested as Spiral.
r.Tassato/Enterio: Magnus Ironarm and his Jotun died at Duarte's Repose.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: The last of the Temeschwari vyig were killed in the Broken Wilds.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Druj were defeated at the Silent Glade and the elders of Peytaht saved.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: The Druj were broken at Oakenclough, though Circe was killed. The ghosts at the Shrine of Hope were soothed and the shrine consecrated to Ambition.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: Varag Soulflayer was killed at Garstang Thicket.
r.Upwold/Tower March: Benson's Orchard was consecrated to Vigilance.
r.Weirwater/Sandling: Areloe Larmallevés investigated strange events at Surlac, and what she found is known only to her.
r.Weirwater/Wickmoor: The Champion of Dawn defeated the Deadwood Knight in the woods bordering Karov.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Dripping Echoes of the Fen was cast in Proceris.

385YE Autumn Equinox winds of war.d: The Military Council was to choose two of three battle opportunities: capturing Sarra Grubfeast in the Salt Flats of Sanath, stopping the Druj and their Winter eternal ally securing magical allies in the Barrens, and capturing the Blue Eel banner and ransoming Mathilda Fisher from the Jotun and yegarra in Tromsa. Each battle needed 136 to 145 force weight from the nations listed. Conjunctions included many attempts to stop heralds across Imperial territories, ventures in Tromsa, and encounters with Quiet Charlie, the Drake's Dozen and the Company of the Torch. Standing considerations covered billeting in Upwold and Mitwold, Marcher and Wintermark bonuses, a Varushkan penalty, and modifiers for fighting between Morrow and Zenith.

n.Dawn: Dawn could send a force weight of 49 to the battles, and Dawnish armies remained unable to take the Cautious Advance or Give Ground orders.
n.Druj: The Druj were the opposition in two of the three battle opportunities: protecting Sarra Grubfeast in the Salt Flats of Sanath, and seeking magical allies with their Winter eternal ally in the Barrens.
n.Highguard: Highguard could send a force weight of 22, and Highborn armies gained bonuses when attacking into Zenith from Morrow or defending Morrow against attacks from Zenith.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: the Imperial Orcs were listed with a force weight of 6 available for the battles.
n.Jotun: The Jotun, alongside yegarra, were the opposition in the Tromsa battle opportunity, where the Empire hoped to seize the Blue Eel banner and ransom Mathilda Fisher from them; Wintermark armies fighting them also had special modifiers.
n.Navarr: Navarr could send a force weight of 51 to the battles, and the Navarr-held territory of Hercynia was the site of a conjunction to stop the heralds.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast could send a force weight of 20; its armies' presence in a campaign reduced Varushkan victory points, and a conjunction to stop the heralds was set in Segura.
n.The League: The League could send a force weight of 19, and League territories hosted conjunctions to balance a debt in Sarvos and deal with the Company of the Torch in Temeschwar.
n.The Marches: The Marches could send a force weight of 24; Marcher armies could not Give Ground but gained 1000 strength in Upwold, Mitwold and Mournwold, and the Strong Reeds gained 1000 strength in Bregasland until the Winter Solstice.
n.Urizen: Urizen could send a force weight of 15, and Urizen armies gained bonuses when attacking Zenith from Morrow or defending Morrow against attacks from Zenith.
n.Varushka: Varushka could send a force weight of 14; its armies generated fewer victory points when campaigning alongside Brass Coast or Wintermark armies, but could take the Hospitality of the Boyars order in Ossium.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark had the largest force weight at 61; its armies could take Fight with Honour and, when fighting the Jotun, gained more victory points and took fewer casualties but inflicted fewer.

t.Bastion: A Saturday conjunction at the Broken Holt in Sybella Cross sought to stop the heralds, with the Senator for Bastion responsible.
t.Bregasland: A Friday conjunction at Harry's Field in Gravenmarch sought to stop the heralds, and the Strong Reeds gained 1000 strength while fighting in Bregasland.
t.Hahnmark: A Saturday conjunction at White Owl Fields in Kronemark sought to stop the heralds, with the Imperial Seer responsible.
t.Hercynia: A Saturday conjunction at Danwyn's Coppice in Northpines sought to stop the heralds, with the Spear of the Seven responsible.
t.Karov: A Saturday conjunction at the Thicket of Nieshka in Wieliczka sought to stop the heralds, with the General of the Eastern Sky responsible.
t.Karsk: A Friday conjunction at Gulgisaz in Nitrost sought to stop the heralds, with the Warden of the Trees and Hills responsible.
t.Mitwold: Any Imperial army could take the Billet order in Mitwold, and Marcher armies fighting there gained an additional 1000 strength.
t.Morrow: A conjunction at Seneca's Meadow in Peregro sought to stop the heralds, and Highborn or Urizen armies defending Morrow against attacks from Zenith gained a defensive bonus.
t.Mournwold: Two conjunctions were set here, one to confront Quiet Charlie in Southmoor and one to talk to Hap the Soft in Green March, and Marcher armies fighting in Mournwold gained 1000 strength.
t.Ossium: Varushkan armies in Ossium could take the Hospitality of the Boyars order.
t.Redoubt: A Saturday conjunction at Magnus' Thicket in Tomari sought to stop the heralds, with the Grandmaster of the Unfettered Mind responsible.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: A Saturday-only battle opportunity offered Imperial heroes the chance to capture Sarra Grubfeast from the Druj here.
t.Sarangrave: A Saturday conjunction at the Queen's Claim in Nesustak Forest aimed to reclaim the Vate's Shelter, with the Advisor on the Vallorn responsible.
t.Sarvos: A Friday conjunction, with combat unlikely, at Bertram's Square in Cigno aimed to balance the debt, with the Dramaturgists of the League responsible.
t.Segura: A Friday conjunction for up to 70 people on the Path to Cerevado in Lucksprings sought to stop the heralds, with the Custodian of the Cerevado Nets responsible.
t.Skarsind: A Friday conjunction at Oathwright's Glade in Gildermark sought to stop the heralds, with the Weigher of Worth responsible.
t.Temeschwar: A Saturday conjunction at Polseg Woods in Vardstein Vale aimed to deal with the Company of the Torch, with the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild responsible.
t.The Barrens: A battle opportunity sought to stop the Druj and their Winter eternal ally securing magical allies here, and a conjunction in Murderdale aimed to slay the Lady of the Dappled Trees.
t.Tromsa: A Sunday battle opportunity against the Jotun and yegarra aimed to capture the Blue Eel banner and ransom Mathilda Fisher, alongside three Friday conjunctions in Tromsdalen, Rikskog and Icewood.
t.Upwold: A conjunction at Tom's Dale in The Heath aimed to deal with the Drake's Dozen; any Imperial army could Billet in Upwold, and Marcher armies there gained 1000 strength.
t.Zenith: Highborn or Urizen armies attacking into Zenith from Morrow gained a 20% bonus to territory captured but inflicted 10% fewer casualties.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: Sixty Imperial heroes could travel to the Broken Holt on Saturday to stop the heralds, under the oversight of the Senator for Bastion.
r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Up to 65 heroes could travel to Harry's Field on Friday night to stop the heralds, with the Keeper of the Dour Fens responsible.
r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: Sixty heroes could travel to White Owl Fields on Saturday evening to stop the heralds, with the Imperial Seer responsible.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: Sixty heroes could travel to Danwyn's Coppice on Saturday to stop the heralds, with the Spear of the Seven responsible.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Thirty heroes could travel to Seneca's Meadow on Friday to stop the heralds, with the Churnspire Adjutor responsible.
r.Mournwold/Green March: A small group of seven could travel to Golden Hoof Farm on Saturday to talk to Hap the Soft, with Bloodcrow Knott responsible and combat unlikely.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: Thirty heroes could travel to the Crowned Trees on Friday night to confront Quiet Charlie, with Brother Martin Orchard responsible.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Sixty heroes could travel to Magnus' Thicket on Saturday to stop the heralds, with the Grandmaster of the Unfettered Mind responsible.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: Sixty heroes could travel to the Queen's Claim on Saturday night to reclaim the Vate's Shelter, with the Advisor on the Vallorn responsible.

r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Thirty heroes could travel to Oathwright's Glade on Friday to stop the heralds, with the Weigher of Worth responsible.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: Thirty heroes could travel to Polseg Woods on Saturday to deal with the Company of the Torch, with the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild responsible.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Sixty heroes could travel to Hugh's Sward on Saturday night to slay the Lady of the Dappled Trees, with the Knight-protector of Spring responsible.
r.Tromsa/Icewood: Sixty heroes could travel to the Grove of Einar on Friday to claim Grimnir's Glass, with the Grimnir of Wittal Grove responsible.
r.Tromsa/Rikskog: Fifty heroes could travel to Fniskard Copse on Friday to claim the Jotun cache, with the Champion of Prosperity responsible.
r.Tromsa/Tromsdalen: Fifty heroes could travel to Nordbotn on Friday to hold the palisade, with the Champion of Pride responsible.
r.Upwold/The Heath: Twenty-five heroes could travel to Tom's Dale on Saturday to deal with the Drake's Dozen, with the Bailiff of the Grand Market responsible.

A question of loyalty.d: The Urizen Assembly's mandate urging Urizen to stay apart from Apulian until a reckoning was supported by the Loyalty Assembly, whose Eyes of Loyalty turned simmering resentment into open secession. Three factions now stand together. Tiborion wants the Imperial Mint moved from Tassato to Cargo as an Urizen seat. Caela demands that Spiral be returned to Urizen. Actius seeks a Treasury-funded office paying 35 thrones a season for Vale of Shadows, using Sung's boon. Sung's shrouds make the rebels nearly impossible to bring to heel. Further mandates could spread the rebellion across Spiral or into Urizen, and the Black Plateau may stir.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's earlier cession of Spiral and Feroz is described as buying time to defeat the Druj, and Spiral's Urizen are noted as having endured Druj attacks.
n.Grendel: If the Senate returned Spiral to Urizen, Kaliact's followers would turn on her, and Apulian, Apulus and Apstrus would revert to Grendel control. Many in Apulian are still legally Grendel.
n.The League: The League's new hold on Spiral faces armed secession, and its Assembly's pledged reckoning is tested by demands such as giving up the Mint at Tassato. Its Assembly may propose mandates to influence its own people in Spiral.
n.Urizen: Urizen citizens in Spiral split by loyalty: some are moving to Zenith and Redoubt, while others have taken up arms. Further mandates could spread the rebellion across Spiral or, if the Empire uses force, into the rest of Urizen.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: the rebels recall the Wintermark thane Dogri Thulebane, who was dragged to Anvil for execution after an earlier secession.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: it was given to the Grendel along with Spiral in the peace treaty that Urizen loyalists resent.
t.Redoubt: Empire-loyal Urizen are relocating here, and Tiborion's faction proposes a Senate commission to build a new Imperial Mint in Cargo as an Urizen national seat.
t.Spiral: Rebel spires have seized Ankra and Cinion and declared them Urizen. Sung's Vale of Shadows hides them from Imperial armies, and unrest risks rousing the Black Plateau.
t.Tassato: Tassato would lose the Imperial Mint, decommissioned there and re-established in Cargo, if the Senate accepted Tiborion's proposed reckoning.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Senate's earlier motion asking Naomi to appraise the septs of the Barrens failed.
t.Zenith: Many Spiral Urizen loyal to the Empire are moving here, and mithril statues on the passes from Spiral are to link the spires with Zenith and Redoubt.

r.Spiral/Ankra: Rebels have seized Ankra and declared it part of Urizen. It is home to Tiborion of the Endless Horizen, who leads the faction seeking the Mint's move.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Apstrus would fall back under Grendel control alongside Apulian if the Senate returned Spiral to Urizen.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus would revert to Grendel control if Spiral were restored to Urizen and Kaliact's followers turned on her.
r.Spiral/Ateri: Rebels in Ateri could rise and seize the region if a further Synod mandate urges the remaining Spiral Urizen to take up arms, unless an Imperial army stops them.
r.Spiral/Cinion: Rebel spires have seized Cinion, declared it Urizen and rejected the authority of the Imperial Senate.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Outraged spires here are preparing for rebellion, and a further mandate could see them seize the region unless an Imperial army intervenes.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Black Plateau at Screed's heart may stir again if the situation escalates, and rebels here could seize the region under a further mandate.

A tale told.d: Wintermark's Bloodcloaks and Green Shield, the Imperial Orc Summer Storm, the Marcher Strong Reeds, Tusks and Bounders, and the Freeborn Fire of the South gathered at Kalant in Stark. About seventy thousand troops took Icewood, Skyfall Waste and Rikskog. At Viheltavathorn, Jarls Olgaf and Klarra died holding the gates, and Mathilda Fisher was mortally wounded. Around fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers died. Igya Olgafsdottir, now Jarl, held Oksenesfestsal. She offered an honour battle at Crows Field for Mathilda's Blue Eel Banner. The Jotun formed three fyrds. A huge Kalsean host retook Skallahn and threatened to cut the Imperial line of retreat.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Oksenesfestsal is compared to Astolat's Castle of Thorns and Semmerholm's Adamant Gate, and the Bound King is noted to have aided the Dawnish in the past.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm, joined by Summer heralds and emissaries of the Shadowed Fire, helped conquer Skyfall Waste and flank the Jotun at Viheltavathorn. Its orcs found the voices of warlike ancestors such as Sjöfn of the Bittenblade clearer in Tromsa.
n.Jotun: The Jotun lost three regions of Tromsa, Viheltavathorn and Jarl Olgaf, while Igya Olgafsdottir took up the jarldom and held Oksenesfestsal. Meanwhile all the armies of Kalsea retook Skallahn and stood ready to strike north or into Sermersuaq.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Bound King is said to have sent his court to aid the Navarr in the past.
n.The Brass Coast: The Fire of the South force-marched from Kahraman to fight in Rikskog, suffering in the northern cold. The Bound King's knights who accompanied the Freeborn ignored their general's orders by executing the fallen, cutting down fugitives and targeting healers.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the unscalable walls of Holberg are cited as an example of defences that could not hold off seventy thousand troops.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the adamant in Oksenesfestsal is compared to that of the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: The Bloodcloaks and Green Shield led the invasion from Stark, and the Jotun repaid their honourable fighting by holding back from killing, which reduced Winterfolk casualties. Igya addressed the Winterfolk at the parley and entrusted General Osric with a knife for Mathilda Fisher.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Oksenesfestsal is described as a match for Astolat's Castle of Thorns.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Mathilda Fisher fled north to Tromsa after her defeat in Bregasland, and the Strong Reeds' general boasts of running the Jotun and Fisher out of it.
t.Fjorknae: Mentioned in passing: Jarl Igya threatened to spirit Mathilda Fisher away to Fjorknae and bury her there if the Empire failed to take her banner.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: its unscalable walls are cited as defences that could not long withstand seventy thousand troops.
t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: the Fishers did not return to their lands in Hordalant, and Jotun embassies to the realms like the Icewood fane have been seen there.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched north from Kahraman, where the Bound King was allowed to slake his hunger in return for his aid.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the Court of the White Fountain in Redoubt is cited as another adamant construction.
t.Sea of Snow: Mentioned in passing: what little the Empire knew of Tromsa came largely from the recent expedition to map the Sea of Snow.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Oksenesfestsal's adamant is compared to the Adamant Gate in Semmerholm.
t.Sermersuaq: Sermersuaq was the staging ground where the seven armies gathered before crossing into Tromsa. It now faces a possible Jotun raid from the Kalsean host massed in Skallahn.
t.Skallahn: Three Imperial armies withdrew from Skallahn to join the invasion, and an immense Jotun force including all the armies of Kalsea then recaptured all the territory the Empire had claimed there. That force is poised to march north into Tromsa or raid Sermersuaq.
t.Tromsa: The Empire captured Icewood, Skyfall Waste and Rikskog of the presumed seven regions, destroyed Viheltavathorn and besieged Oksenesfestsal, while Jarl Olgaf fell and his daughter Igya succeeded him. Three Jotun fyrds rallied in the west.
t.Tsirku: Mentioned in passing: Tsirku lies north of the Skyfall Wastes, Lake Karnakadatha sits on its border, and its proximity may explain Tromsa's strangeness.

r.Sermersuaq/Stark: The Imperial armies and their realm allies mustered at the Fortress of Kalant in Stark before crossing the Lansipari into Tromsa.
r.Skallahn/Eyrarfell: Mentioned in passing: the mountains of Tromsdalen are part of the same range as Eyrarfell.
r.Skallahn/Iron Stand: Mentioned in passing: the Summer Storm, Bloodcloaks and Green Shield withdrew out of Iron Stand into Sermersuaq before the invasion.
r.Tromsa/Icewood: Icewood was the first region conquered, as Jarl Bjørnda Bearcrusher retreated west with her warriors and thralls. In the north, a fane of Wise Rangara was found and left under watch by a hundred Imperial soldiers.
r.Tromsa/Majastind: Mentioned in passing: thralls describe Mount Majastind at the heart of Tromsa as the throne of the gods, but the region was not reached.
r.Tromsa/Rikskog: Rikskog was taken after the Battle of Viheltavathorn, where the fortified tower was destroyed, Jarls Olgaf and Klarra died and Mathilda Fisher was mortally wounded. Jotun remain at Fniskard's Palisade, and a Jotun recapture of the region could cut off the Imperial retreat.
r.Tromsa/Skyfall Waste: Jarl Hodne Hodnesson's hall, Hodnesshal, fell and the storm-swept tundra was conquered. This gave the Empire Lake Karnakadatha, an ilium source the Senate could allocate if the region is held.
r.Tromsa/Tromsdalen: The Imperial advance stalled before the adamant-reinforced Oksenesfestsal, held by Igya Olgafsdottir, leaving the region one tenth captured. Jotun reinforcements were moving through the Nordbotn pass to resupply the fortress.

A walk in shadow.d: The Urizeni Citadel Guard led the crossing with the Irresistible Spear. Summer knights fought alongside the Dawnish and Urizeni armies, and the Iron Helms waged a merciless onslaught of terror. Five Druj armies under the White Lion, reinforced from the city of Leen, pushed the Empire back. Over fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers died, and perhaps twice as many Druj. Imperial forces were a tenth of the way to capturing the Fens. A potent miasma and a Night shroud lay over the territory. The page also set out three opportunities: intercepting the captive former governor Sarra Grubfeast at the Brineways, warding the Well of Tears against Skathe, and stopping a Druj band heading into Brocéliande.

n.Dawn: Dawn's Gryphon's Pride, under Archavion Wolfborne, marched into the Mallum for the third time with Summer knights at its side. Dawn's Barrens faced Winter husks raised against it, and its Knight-protector of Spring was charged with slaying the Lady of the Dappled Trees.
n.Druj: The Druj defended their heartland under White Lion command and pushed the Empire back to the river at heavy cost. They hold Grubfeast captive for judgement in Leen and are plotting with Skathe and Yaw'nagrah from Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht.
n.Highguard: The Highborn Valiant Pegasus, under Jack Flint, gathered intelligence from the surrendered Vendarri and fought in the Fens. Highguard's leaders could see Grubfeast handed to the Rahvin to improve relations with that sept.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr had been hunting Sarra Grubfeast in the Sarangrave before she resurfaced in the Salt Flats.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Druj veterans of the fighting in Holberg were among Leen's warriors, and Holberg mercenaries once fought alongside House Bettencourt.
n.Urizen: Urizen's Citadel Guard, under Nicassia Avicia, spearheaded the assault and built the fortified camp that let the Empire cling to the Salt Flats despite the Druj counter-attack.
n.Varushka: The Iron Helms, under Alderei the Fair, were unleashed in a merciless onslaught that spread terror through the Fens. The Leen veterans focused much of their wrath on the Varushkans.

t.Brocéliande: A band of Druj led by the Lady of the Dappled Trees, a herald of Yaw'nagrah, was seen heading through Brocéliande towards Dark Ranging.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride were repulsed there almost two years earlier, and the Empire had no map of it, as with the Salt Flats.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: many Druj from Leen were veterans of past battles in Holberg, and Holberg mercenaries once fought beside House Bettencourt.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Gryphon's Pride conquered it three years earlier, and its miasma was compared with the stronger one in the Salt Flats.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Druj veterans of Reikos fought in the Fens, and accounts of Grubfeast's cruelty made even veterans of Reikos blanch.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Imperial armies invaded for the first time in many decades and were forced back to their riverside camp, but not out. The territory lies under an ancient miasma and a Night shroud, and Grubfeast is being taken across it to Leen.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: the Navarr hunted Grubfeast there, and the ghulai Tankath Seveneyes left its Palace of the Sleepers carrying notes on a ritual text being codified there.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: its claiming for the Empire preceded House Bettencourt's ill-fated push into the Barrens.
t.The Barrens: The armies staged from the Barrens, where Druj-held regions threaten to use the Well of Tears to raise Winter spirits. That would leave the whole territory contested unless the regio is warded.
t.The Semmerlak: Mentioned in passing: the Nameless River connects the Semmerlak to the Barren Sea, the Feverwater and the open sea.
t.Therunin: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page notes only that the Nameless River links to the Feverwater and on to the sea.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: the miasma in the Salt Flats was noted as more potent than the one Imperial armies met in Zenith.

r.Brocéliande/Dark Ranging: Druj warriors with the Lady of the Dappled Trees were seen by yeofolk making their way towards Dark Ranging.
r.Salt Flats of Sanath/Sydathian Fens: The Fens were the battlefield, a miasma-cloaked marsh ruled by the Razorbird clan, where over fifteen hundred Imperial soldiers died. The Empire ended the season a tenth of the way to capturing the region.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Mentioned in passing: not named directly; the page refers only to the wider Barrens, which Winter spirits could overrun if the Well of Tears is not warded.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: It remains in Druj hands, and some of its Druj joined the band heading for Brocéliande. The page notes it holds no regio linked to Skathe.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Still Druj-held, Murderdale could be fortified by Skathe's hungry ghosts, equivalent to a 2000-strength fortification, if the Well of Tears is not warded. The Sentinel Gate was to open to Hugh's Sward there.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The four armies gathered at Saltmarsh to ford the Nameless River. Its Vendarri sept, nominally surrendered to the Highborn, briefed the Valiant Pegasus on what lay beyond.

A wisdom of questions.d: At the Summer Solstice, Herminius's statement that sword scholars should no longer venerate Sulemaine passed the Urizen Assembly 374-16. A 75-liao mandate carried by a known sword scholar could now separate the teachings from the woman. That would shatter the Temple of the Four Winds, drive Sulemainists such as Severus away, and cost every Urizen congregation 2 votes and 1 liao for a year, because it reverses the Assembly's 383YE praise of her. Sulemaine's tomb was not consecrated, to Highborn relief, but some Highborn proposed a writ of consecration needing Synod approval. Cato and Clytemnestra will teach at Laroc, and a Dawnish mandate could spread their questioning ethos there.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish Assembly could send 50 liao to urge the faithful to learn at Laroc. Over time this would mean Synod mandates only affect Dawn if passed by a greater majority, but it would also bring questioning of the noble houses and a threat to the discipline of Dawnish armies.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Highborn histories describe their triumph over Sulemaine's creed in the same terms as victories over the Druj.
n.Highguard: Highborn histories treat those Sulemaine killed as martyrs, and Highguard was relieved that her tomb was not consecrated. Some Highborn priests proposed a writ of consecration that would require approval by a Virtue assembly and the General Assembly.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: sword scholars already teach at the Scholars of the Sword Academy in Holberg.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly could send a known sword scholar to separate the movement from Sulemaine. Doing so would cause an irreversible schism, close the Temple of the Four Winds and weaken all Urizen congregations for a year.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: the Synod's influence, weakened by earlier sword scholar campaigns, is still diminished in Varushka.

t.Astolat: Cato and Clytemnestra of the House of the Wanderer accepted Ser Dindrane de Cantharos's invitation to teach at the small Cathedral of Laroc. A Dawnish mandate could make Laroc a source of sword scholar ideas for the whole nation.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: sword scholars were previously invited to teach in Holberg, at the Scholars of the Sword Academy.

Back in town.d: Meraud declined parley but offered Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés plans for the Flame of the Phoenix, a mana-producing sinecure in Astolat. It must be commissioned by the end of the Winter Solstice and ceded to him. Zakalwe arranged a parley with Skywise Gralka, and his myrmidons began aiding the fight against Cold Sun. Prospero responded privately and offered a Runesmith's Law schema in return for ten rings of ilium and a ritual text. Tharim sent courtiers to speak with named citizens and agreed to empower a Throne-linked ritual. Janon arranged a parley and proposed an Imperial title. Arhallogen, angered by the Spring Archmage's tone, would receive only five Navarr vates.

n.Dawn: Meraud offered Enchantress Areloe Larmallevés plans for the Flame of the Phoenix in Astolat, and its Tender would gain extra powers and a ministry if they were a Dawnish noble Enchanter. Enchantress Armand Remys was among those Tharim's courtiers would visit.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen's herald acknowledged that the eternal continues to aid the Druj.
n.Highguard: Zakalwe's three myrmidon messengers joined the garrison of the Silent Sentinel to support Highguard's defence of Casinea against Cold Sun.
n.Navarr: Arhallogen would receive only Navarr vates, no more than five, and claimed his role in their treaty with the Mallum orcs had spared Therunin. Prospero was watching whether the Navarr would keep Thornsong House's apothecary lore for themselves.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Meraud suggested that Marsello Givello Cellini di Sarvos speak to the Warlocks of Otkodov.
n.Urizen: Zakalwe's myrmidons were especially common in Urizen, citing a debt to the mountain people who saved them from extinction. The Urizen Archmages of Winter and Night secured meetings with Tharim's courtiers and Janon.
n.Wintermark: Prospero offered a schema for inclusion in Runesmith's Law, to be given to the smiths of Runegrott, and approved of Wintermark artisans keeping their own unique lore.

t.Astolat: Meraud proposed building the Flame of the Phoenix at a regio near the Larmallevés estate. Prospero's minotaur herald also appeared at the Castle of Thorns.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen declared that nothing at the Heart of the Tempest is any longer of interest to eternals of the Endless Forest.
t.Casinea: Three of Zakalwe's myrmidons joined the garrison at the Silent Sentinel to help defend Casinea against Cold Sun.
t.Hahnmark: Prospero's schema for Runesmith's Law would be given to the smiths at Runegrott if the Archmage of Autumn met his terms.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: Meraud suggested consulting the Warlocks of Otkodov on a matter raised by Marsello Givello Cellini di Sarvos.
t.Therunin: Arhallogen claimed that his involvement in the Navarr treaty with the Mallum orcs saved Therunin from despoilment like Zenith's. He also scorned the 'cowards of the Great Forest' sheltering there.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Arhallogen cited Zenith's despoilment as the fate Therunin had escaped.

Between two mounds.d: After the Freeborn raised a mound over the Jotun champions who died at Fort Braydon, a ghodi speaking for King Gudmundur of Narkyst sought leave to build a fire-filled bowl from nine wains of mithril honouring the Freeborn. The Assembly could allow it, turn her back, guard her, or let the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills raid Liathaven to seize her and the mithril. She also asked why the Freeborn fight alongside servants of the King in Chains. In Tromsa, Jarl Ustigar asked Generals Iron Osric and Lofyn Blood-Cloak to swear that no ally would loot Majastind, resting place of Ulven. Any of the seven armies there could loot it this season. Meanwhile almost a thousand Sermersuaq thralls were freed.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun King asks why the Freeborn fight 'like the Druj' and march alongside corrupted knights bound to the King in Chains.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Jarls fear that the Imperial Orcs, who grow ever closer to their own ancestors, might seek out Mount Majastind to steal the Jotun ancestors. Their army in Tromsa is one of those that could choose to loot it.
n.Jotun: The Jotun reached out on two fronts. The King of Narkyst sought to honour his fallen champions and questioned Freeborn honour, while the Jarl of Kierheim pleaded for the safety of Mount Majastind, where Ulven and many ancestors lie with great treasures and artefacts.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn had to decide whether to permit, refuse, guard or plunder the ghodi's mithril monument. They were also challenged by the King of Narkyst to explain why they raise barrows for Jotun dead yet fight beside servants of the King in Chains.
n.The Marches: The Jarls distrust the Marchers in Tromsa despite their recent efforts to reclaim their honour, because they unleashed curses on their own people in the Mournwold barely half a decade before.
n.Wintermark: Generals Iron Osric and Lofyn Blood-Cloak were asked to swear an oath before the egregores that their allies would not despoil Mount Majastind. Separately, the thralls taken from Sermersuaq were returned under a deal struck with the General of the Green Shield.

t.Hordalant: Mentioned in passing: some Sermersuaq thralls had been made to work Jotun estates in Hordalant before their release.
t.Kahraman: The Freeborn raised a burial mound over the Jotun dead here. An unarmed ghodi then studied it and announced plans to return after the Autumn Equinox to build a burning mithril monument, unless the Assembly mandated otherwise.
t.Kallavesa: The Jarl of Kierheim compared Majastind to the sacred marshes of Kallavesa and implied that the marshes could face Ulvenwar reprisals if the Jotun tombs were looted.
t.Liathaven: The ghodi was expected to carry nine wains of mithril through Liathaven, where the Dhomiro of the Cinnabar Hills could order a lightning raid to capture her and the metal.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the deaths of thralls in the Mournwold are cited as the stain on Jotun honour that keeps the King from making peace.
t.Sermersuaq: Almost a thousand thralls taken from Sermersuaq during the Jotun conquest were released and escorted in good health to Olgafsdottirshal, to great celebration.
t.Skallahn: Mentioned in passing: some Sermersuaq thralls had been made to work Jotun estates in Skallahn before their release.
t.Tromsa: With Imperial armies invading, the new Jarl Igya Olgafsdottir refused to yield and offered battle to capture Mathilda Fisher. The Jarl of Kierheim came north to plead for Mount Majastind.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The burial mound of the Jotun champions stands here, and it is where the ghodi proposed to raise her ever-burning mithril bowl honouring the Freeborn.
r.Tromsa/Majastind: Mount Majastind holds Ulven's bones, many other ancestors, great wealth and at least three artefacts. An Imperial army fighting in Tromsa that targeted the region this season could loot it, unless Wintermark's oath prevented this.

Construct Bright-Threads Brass Works.d: Announced by Groza, the Legion Engineer, in Autumn 385YE, the Bright-Threads Brass Works was a sinecure to be built in Valasmark in Hahnmark, providing orichalcum. Construction cost 10 wains of mithril and 30 crowns on top of standard costs, and took three months. After the Autumn Equinox, Deorlaf Bright Thread supplied the 10 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns. With the work completed, the tenured position of Bright Threadweaver was created, elected by unanimous decision of Wintermark's senators, and was first filled at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.Wintermark: Wintermark gained a new tenured title, Bright Threadweaver, chosen by the unanimous decision of its senators, after the Wintermark citizen Deorlaf Bright Thread funded the works.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark became home to a new orichalcum-producing sinecure, the Bright-Threads Brass Works, completed after three months.

r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: The Bright-Threads Brass Works was built in Valasmark, giving the region a working source of orichalcum attached to the Bright Threadweaver title.

Construct Holberg's Melodious Cascade.d: The sinecure cost 10 wains of mithril and 30 crowns of labour and took three months to build. It was self-funded by Bernhard and Lula Kleist von Ennerlund and other League citizens, whose names were to be inscribed near the cascade's entrance; the commission credited Abigail Ashill and Theodora von Holberg as inspiration. Lula Kleist von Ennerlund provided 9 wains of mithril and 3 thrones 6 crowns, and Otmar van Holberg the final wain. The cascade created the post of Director of Holberg's Melodious Cascade, appointed annually by the League's senators and revocable by the Assembly of Nine, the General Assembly and the League National Assembly. The first appointment was due at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.The League: The League gained a new national position, the Director of Holberg's Melodious Cascade, appointed annually by its senators and first available at the Winter Solstice 385YE, with League citizens paying for the work themselves.

t.Holberg: Holberg gained a new sinecure, the Melodious Cascade, producing nine mana each season and celebrated by its builders as a tribute to their great city.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the commission was announced by Laughlan vi Temeschwar, the Master of Rings, whose name references the territory.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The Melodious Cascade was built in Holmauer, with the names of the League citizens who supplied its mithril to be inscribed near its entrance.

Construct Kurstrozi's Lumbermill.d: Framed as making use of unused wealth in hard times, the commission was announced by the Master of the Koboldi. The announcement said it would be fully funded by Krasivit Buhkova. It required 40 wains of white granite and 15 thrones, plus standard costs, and would take three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox, Oleinsky Kasprzak provided the 40 wains of white granite and 13 thrones 6 crowns. Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn, Kostjya and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov gave smaller sums of crowns. Once built, the lumbermill will distribute a share of 20 random materials to the Varushkan forest owners of Ossium.

n.Varushka: A Varushkan great work commissioned by the Master of the Koboldi and funded by Varushkan contributors, it will benefit the nation's forest owners in Ossium with a share of 20 random materials.

t.Ossium: Kurstrozi's Lumbermill is to be built at Drownbark to increase the prosperity of Ossium's forests, sharing 20 random materials among the Varushkan forest owners there.

Construct Townsend Treasury.d: Using the authority of an Imperial Wayleave, Bertrand announced the commission of a money sinecure named the Townsend Treasury in Sarcombe, Mournwold. Its holder, the Town Clerk of Sarcombe, is a Marcher national title appointed annually by unanimous vote of the Marcher senators at the Winter Solstice. The work cost 10 wains of white granite and 30 crowns plus standard costs, and took three months. Morgan Townsend von Holberg met the costs after the Autumn Equinox 385YE, providing 3 thrones, 6 crowns and the granite. The Treasury was completed, and the Marcher senators first appointed a Town Clerk of Sarcombe at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.The Marches: The Marches gained a new national title, the Town Clerk of Sarcombe, which its senators must fill each Winter Solstice by unanimous vote. They made the first appointment at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

t.Mournwold: The Townsend Treasury was raised in Sarcombe in the Mournwold, paid for in full by Morgan Townsend von Holberg, and was completed by Winter 385YE.

Construct the Deep Place.d: Proposed by the senator for Volodmartz and seconded by Miekarova, the motion took up a time-limited opportunity from the wind of fortune The horror and the wild. It built a ministry in Volodmartz costing 10 wains of white granite, 5 wains of mithril and 45 crowns, taking three months to complete. After the Autumn Equinox 385YE Marzanna Verchernyaya Zorya supplied the granite, Victor Gryllian the mithril and most of the money, with further coin from Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Iskra Marzenanova Navratil. With the work completed, the senators of Varushka could appoint the first Bredavoi Emissary at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained a new ministry in its own lands, and its senators received the right to elect the Bredavoi Emissary, first appointable at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

t.Volodmartz: Volodmartz's senator proposed the motion, and the territory became home to new mine workings meant to aid the cabalists of Void while keeping vigilance over them.

r.Volodmartz/Brez: The mountains of Brez were the site of the Deep Place, the mine workings built to support and watch over the cabalists of Void.

Construct the Five Cities Military Acade.d: Proposed by the senator for Tassato and seconded by Astolat, the motion funded the Five Cities Military Academy in Tassato under the terms of the Schools and sawmills Wind of Fortune. Construction required 30 wains of white granite, 30 wains of mithril and 180 crowns, and took six months. Several individuals paid for it between Autumn 385YE and Autumn 386YE. The largest share, including all the mithril and most of the white granite, came in two instalments from Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato. Rodrigo Barossa de Tassato Regario, Rafael Barossa d'Apulian and others gave smaller sums. With the academy complete, the League can now support three armies.

n.The League: The completed academy raised the number of armies the League can support to three, and League citizens such as Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato supplied most of the materials and money.

t.Tassato: Tassato's senator proposed the motion, and the territory gained the Five Cities Military Academy as a new folly.

r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: The Five Cities Military Academy was built in Tassato Mestra, taking six months to complete.

Construct the Gates of Holmauer Park.d: Announced by Elsha Bertolf, Chair of the Wolf, the great work followed the Dear green space Wind of Fortune and was inspired by a Summer 384YE judgement of the Cardinal of Wisdom, Hembeneth i Guerra. It cost 20 wains of mithril and 60 crowns and took three months to complete. It was self-funded by League citizens: Lula and Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund gave six wains of mithril each, Lula also providing the coin, while Magdalena Teyhard von Holberg, Otmar van Holberg, Victor van Holberg and Taskel Di Apulian gave two wains each. With the gates complete, the expected influx of paying tourists increases the seasonal production of Holberg's businesses by 36 rings.

n.The League: League citizens privately funded the great work, announced by the Chair of the Wolf, and League business owners in Holberg now benefit from the tourist trade it draws.

t.Holberg: Holberg gained a completed great work that raises the seasonal production of its businesses by 36 rings through paying visitors to Holmauer Park.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: Holmauer Park's eight gates are now secured with mithril and its visitors are protected by a small garrison supported by local magicians and priests.

Construct the Greenwatch.d: Proposed by Reikos and seconded by Hercynia, the motion ordered construction of the Greenwatch in Casinea. The ministry strengthens those who fight the vallorn, especially those who must venture into the vallorn miasma, and carries all responsibilities required by Ossegrahn, the Rain Lord. It cost 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns and took three months to build. Contributions came from several donors after the Autumn Equinox and Winter Solstice 385YE, including Melkior of Balthazar's Vineyard, who supplied 6 thrones and all 20 wains of white granite. With the building complete, the Senators of Highguard could appoint the first Greenwatcher at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

n.Highguard: Highguard gained a new national title, the Greenwatcher, appointed annually by its Senators, with the first appointment available at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

t.Casinea: The Greenwatch was built in Casinea as a ministry to strengthen those fighting the vallorn and entering its miasma.

Construct the Lakesedge Highway.d: Proposed by the senator for Holberg and seconded by Segura, the motion commissioned a sinecure in Holberg under the Schools and sawmills Wind of Fortune. It required 30 wains of white granite, 54 crowns and three months' work. After the Autumn Equinox the materials and money came from several donors, chiefly Gideon of the suns of Couros with 25 wains of white granite, along with Otmar van Holberg, Lia Adelaar, Jonah Yakovitch, Bernhard Kleist von Ennerlund, Claus Friedrich von Holberg, Cees Van Holberg and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov. The highway was completed, and the Rebeshof Roadwarden was to be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE for a limited term.
