n.The League: The League gained a new Imperial title, the Rebeshof Roadwarden, which its senators elect each year, with the first appointment due at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

t.Holberg: Holberg received a new highway, proposed by its own senator, running from the Holmauer Gate through Rebeshof to Misericorde.

r.Holberg/Holmauer: The new highway begins at the Holmauer Gate, linking Holmauer to Rebeshof and Misericorde.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: Misericorde is the far end of the Lakesedge Highway, now joined by road to the Holmauer Gate through Rebeshof.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The highway runs through Rebeshof, which gives its name to the new Rebeshof Roadwarden title.

Construct the Red Depths.d: Proposed by the senator for Segura and seconded by Weirwater, the motion created a mithril seat in Kahraman, costing 50 thrones, taking three months to build and carrying 10 thrones in seasonal upkeep. Funding came after the Autumn Equinox, with Bakar i Riqueza providing 49 thrones and 6 crowns and Fretek Sargava Slavomiryn and Konstantin Rabovich Bolotnikov a crown each. Disruption caused by the Lasambrian Orcs delayed completion until the Spring Equinox at the earliest. Once finished, the seat is to be allocated by Tally of the Votes among the fleets of the Brass Coast.

n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gains a national mithril Bourse seat paid for by its own citizens, which its fleets will allocate by Tally of the Votes once the delayed construction is finished.

t.Kahraman: The Red Depths are being built in Kahraman, though Lasambrian Orc disruption has delayed their completion until the Spring Equinox at the earliest.

Construct the School of Hard Knocks in T.d: The motion took up the opportunity offered by the Schools and sawmills Wind of Fortune to construct a sinecure in Temeschwar. Besides standard costs, it required 20 wains of white granite and 60 crowns, and took three months to complete. The motion named the new title 'Maestro of Wolves', to be appointed by unanimous decision of League senators. After the Autumn Equinox 385YE, Valentina von Temeshwar provided 7 thrones 4 crowns and the 20 wains of white granite. Once complete, the position, recorded in the outcome as Master of the Sword Academy of Temeschwar, became available for election by the League's senators for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.The League: The League gained a new sinecure title chosen by its own senators, with the first election due at the Winter Solstice 385YE. The project was paid for by Valentina von Temeshwar.

t.Temeschwar: The School of Hard Knocks was built in Temeschwar, giving the territory a new academy and an associated title tied to it.

Construct the Stones from Blood.d: Proposed by Miaren and seconded by the Conscience of the Senate, the motion created a ministry in Therunin for purchasing mana crystals. Its purpose was to help the Navarr vates organise and to supply mana for national rituals such as Dance of Navarr and Thorn. Construction cost 12 wains of mithril and 36 crowns on top of standard costs, and took three months. The materials were provided after the Autumn Equinox by Bledri Eternal (5 wains and 4 thrones 4 crowns), Eleri Bronwen's Rest (5 wains) and Cara (2 wains). With the work complete, the Factor of Stones from Blood would be elected by the senators of Navarr for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.Navarr: The Navarr vates council gained a ministry to support its organisation and to supply mana for national rituals such as Dance of Navarr and Thorn. Navarr senators would elect its Factor from the Winter Solstice 385YE.

t.Therunin: Stones from Blood was built in Therunin as a ministry for purchasing mana crystals, paid for with 12 wains of mithril and 36 crowns.

Construct the Triosk Metal Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Ossium and seconded by Karsk, the motion commissioned the Triosk Metal Exchange and created a title, named in the motion as Merchant-Boyar of the Eagle and Stag Exchange, to be appointed by tally of the votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners, with responsibilities as set out in the Wind of Fortune. Construction cost 16 wains of mithril and 6 thrones and took three months. Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen provided the full mithril and money after the Autumn Equinox 385YE. With the work complete, the title, recorded in the outcome as the Eagle of Triosk, was to be appointed for the first time at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.Varushka: Varushka gained a new ministry whose holder is chosen by the votes of Varushkan mine and forest owners, and a Varushkan, Desilav Sergeyevich Jesen, paid for its construction.

t.Volodmartz: The Triosk Metal Exchange was built in Triosk, Volodmartz, giving the territory a ministry seat whose title was first due to be appointed at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

Dog days are over.d: Following the Earl of Fools' mandate, noble houses agreed on a tourney season running from the Barrens through Semmerholm and Weirwater to Astolat. Any Imperial military unit could join the Grand Tour for a year. Dawnish yeofolk could upgrade farms, forests, mines and herb gardens for one fewer wain. Established troubadours gained four extra crowns per event. Earl Eoric du Borne proposed a School of Music and Poetry at Culwich with a new Reader title. Hugh de Veran proposed restoring the throne room at Withy. Blasine Carver proposed a church and mithril hero statues at Hope's Rest, an opportunity later superseded by the Poetry and Prose wind.

n.Dawn: Dawn celebrated its conquest of the Barrens with a year-long Grand Tour of tourneys, cheaper resource upgrades for yeofolk, higher earnings for troubadours and several proposed commissions to commemorate the triumph.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are described as soundly beaten, and Dawn's heroes are honoured for their final defeat in the Barrens.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a newly ennobled Dawnish lord talks of fighting the Grendel again in the in-character vignette.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: Holberg wine appears in the vignette, and Holberg's merchants are credited with the largest fortification in the Empire.

t.Astolat: Astolat was chosen as the culminating stage of the Grand Tour, and its Castle of Thorns throne room was proposed for restoration.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg red wine is served in the vignette, and Holberg's fortification is called the largest in the Empire.
t.Semmerholm: Semmerholm was to host the second season of the Grand Tour's tourneys, following the Barrens.
t.The Barrens: With its conquest declared complete, the Barrens was to open the Grand Tour's tourney season, and a church honouring the heroes of the conquest was proposed at Hope's Rest.
t.Weirwater: Weirwater was to host the third season of the Grand Tour, and a School of Music and Poetry was proposed at Culwich, supported by its weavers' circles.

r.Astolat/Withy: Hugh de Veran proposed restoring the dilapidated throne room of the Castle of Thorns at a cost of 15 white granite and 45 crowns. Once complete, it would make Dawnish congregation upgrades cheaper for a year and yield historical research on Dawn's early monarchs.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Consecrated with true liao, Hope's Rest drew Dawnish pilgrims, and Blasine Carver proposed a Church of Ser Guineve and mithril statues of the conquest's heroes there. The church would give Dawnish units on adventures a permanent boost, though this opportunity was later superseded by the Poetry and Prose wind.

Dredge the Westmere.d: Proposed by Mitwold's senator and seconded by Kallavesa's, the commission cost 50 wains of weirwood, 30 wains of white granite and 30 thrones, and took six months. Henry Birchsmith supplied most of the materials and money across two seasons, with smaller donations from Watkin, Kostjya, Fintan Nighthaven and others. Once complete, it created the Alder of Meade, a Marcher Bourse position and liaison to the Tseriyn family of Faraden, elected annually by the owners of Marcher farms. It also created the Mediator of Fisk, elected by the commanders of Wintermark's military units. Meade March gained the coastal quality, and seasonal taxation from Bregasland, Kallavesa and Mitwold rose by nine thrones overall.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Jotun is not named on the page, but it held Bregasland, one of the territories listed as contributing to the increase in taxation.
n.The Marches: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion, Marcher donors largely funded it, and the farm owners of the Marches gained the right to elect the Alder of Meade, a new mithril ministry and Bourse position.
n.Wintermark: Kallavesa's senator seconded the motion, and the commanders of Wintermark's military units gained the right to elect the Mediator of Fisk, a new ilium ministry.

t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Bregasland is named among the territories sharing in the overall nine-throne seasonal rise in taxation.
t.Kallavesa: Kallavesa gained an ilium ministry in Fisk, held by the Mediator of Fisk, and shared in the rise in taxation.
t.Mitwold: The Westmere was dredged at Meade March in Mitwold, creating the mithril ministry of the Alder of Meade and raising the territory's taxation.

r.Mitwold/Meade March: Dredging the Westmere gave Meade March the coastal quality, and the region became home to the new mithril ministry held by the Alder of Meade.

Hierarchs of sea and sky.d: Kimus's viziers watched events in every territory. Kimus offered weltsilver-powered Day rituals, crystal repel implements, a boon of finding, a Day-aligned orrery for the Penumbral Watcher's tower and a one-off spy network over the Salt Flats of Sanath. Phaleron offered fact-filled parchments, historical research, a one-time ritual to fortify the libraries at Canterspire or Hacynian, and vallorn tomes for Miaren. Zakalwe offered to assess defences and hone armies, but would not assess Varushka's, and sought an interdiction on savagery enchantments. Sinokenon offered a single appraisal. A reconciled Ylenwe proposed the Canticle Circle in Altis. Leviathan asked for a hall in a historical city.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Meade is named among the 'historical cities' where Leviathan would accept a hall for his heralds.
n.Druj: Kimus dislikes the Druj for their shrouds and secrecy, and offered to help the Shuttered Lantern map the Salt Flats of Sanath, their one territory without an Imperial spy network.
n.Highguard: Ylenwe offered support for the sacred city at Bastion if asked. Leviathan's heralds visited the White City Museum and resented the destruction of the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters in Reikos.
n.Imperial Orcs: Sinokenon's growing interest in the Empire was apparently sparked by the Loyalty of the Imperial Orcs, whom it helped recover the shield Oath-Heart from the Fishers.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Phaleron's historical research, delivered at the Winter Solstice, was published under the title Steinr, Vard, and Jotun.
n.Navarr: Phaleron offered the Advisor on the Vallorn copies of every major vallorn tome, cutting the research into its destruction by three months. Zakalwe criticised the Night magic that gave Navarr armies murderous fervour in Kahraman.
n.The Brass Coast: Zakalwe cited the Fire of the South's recent enchantment as the kind of savagery magic he wants interdicted. Diora University was named among the storehouses of knowledge the Empire must protect.
n.The League: Viziers of Kimus lingered in a League tavern. Leviathan's heralds visited Tassato's museums, and Tassato and Sarvos were offered as sites for a Leviathan Hall.
n.Urizen: Phaleron reaffirmed its support for Urizen lore and offered a one-time ritual to protect the Grand Library of Canterspire. Ylenwe proposed a conservatory of music and mathematics at the Spire of the Canticle.
n.Varushka: Zakalwe refused, without explanation, to assess or hone any Varushkan army.

t.Bastion: Ylenwe offered help building the sacred city, whose designs include great bells. Leviathan's heralds visited the White City Museum, and Bastion was named as a possible site for a Leviathan Hall.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: Kimus noted that the Empire already has a spy network in the Forest of Ulnak.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg University was listed among the great storehouses of knowledge whose loss would void Phaleron's library-defence ritual.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Zakalwe cited the Night magic that made Navarr armies murderously fervent in the recent Kahraman campaign as an example of savagery enchantments.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Diora University was listed among the great storehouses of knowledge whose loss would void Phaleron's library-defence ritual.
t.Miaren: Phaleron offered to deliver its vallorn tomes to the library in Miaren and could protect the Great Library at Hacynian. Miaren was also named as a possible site for a Leviathan Hall.
t.Morrow: Ylenwe offered to help build the Canticle Circle, an auditorium and school of music and mathematics at the Spire of the Canticle, available until the end of the Winter Solstice 385YE.
t.Redoubt: Phaleron provided an arcane projection that could transform the Grand Library at Canterspire into a fortification, though it will never offer the magic again.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: a herald of Leviathan visited the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters before its destruction, which left the eternal quite miffed.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Kimus offered heralds to support a one-off Shuttered Lantern spy network mapping the territory. Units would work two ranks more effectively if the Citadel Guard, already there, used the Technique of the Celestial Key.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: Kimus noted that the Empire already has a spy network in the Sarangrave.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Sarvos was named among the historical cities where Leviathan would accept a hall for his heralds.
t.Segura: Mentioned in passing: a vizier of Kimus sat on a stile in Segura for a month watching sheep and gathering shepherds' songs and stories.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: Meade was named among the historical cities where Leviathan would accept a hall for his heralds.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: Leviathan's heralds visited the Weigher of Worth museum in Skarsind.
t.Tassato: Leviathan's heralds visited the Blood Red River Museum and the Printers' Guild Museum in Tassato, and the city was named as a possible site for a Leviathan Hall.

r.Morrow/Altis: Ylenwe proposed the Canticle Circle near the Spire of the Canticle, costing 30 wains of white granite, 15 wains of mithril and 135 crowns. The edifice would draw musicians, scholars and instrument-makers and house heralds of Ylenwe.

Landscape.d: Heralds of the Bronze Artisan helped the Civil Service survey the area. The Red Depths mithril seam could be an Imperial Bourse seat for 170 thrones producing 16 wains a season, or a national seat for 50 thrones producing 19 wains, because Kahraman's mining families would offer their labour only for a national seat. A Mountainhome ministry, costing 15 white granite and 45 crowns, was proposed so that a mine captain could oversee the weltsilver and orichalcum workings. The House of Fire and Flame sought mining rights through a Declaration of Concord. The Senate approved the Red Depths as a national seat. The work was disrupted by the Lasambrian Jotun but completed, with the title to be first elected at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

n.Jotun: The new mineral wealth makes Serra Damata an even more tempting target for the Jotun. The collapsed passes stop them striking the region directly, but they could still attack through Gambit, and the Lasambrian Jotun disrupted the Red Depths work before the Winter Solstice.
n.The Brass Coast: Kahraman's mining families secured the Red Depths as a national Bourse seat of the Brass Coast, the territory's first mineral wealth kept for its own people. A Mountainhome mine captain was also proposed to keep the feuding families' workings safe.

t.Kahraman: Kahraman gained a national mithril Bourse seat on top of its two Imperial seats. However, with Fort Braydon destroyed, the territory remains largely unprotected, and a rank two or greater fort in Gambit or Serra Damata was urged to deter Jotun attacks.
t.Liathaven: The collapse of the mountain passes means Jotun armies can no longer move between Liathaven and northern Kahraman.
t.Reinos: The blocked passes mean Jotun armies in Reinos can no longer reach northern Kahraman directly.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: Gambit, still under Imperial control, became the likely route for any Jotun assault on Serra Damata. A significant fortification there was recommended to protect the whole territory.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The ruined mountain here holds the Red Depths mithril seam, now a national Bourse seat, along with proposed Mountainhome mines for weltsilver, orichalcum and bloodstones. The House of Fire and Flame also asked for the right to mine here, while the region remains a prime Jotun target.

Not to conquer.d: Ser Dindrane's policy persuaded new Dawnish settlers to hold back while negotiations began, aided by Highborn priests using peerless kinship. Almost every faction understood 'liberation' as having land ceded to it. The Rahvin held the Fangs and wanted three regions. The Karass, already foreigners, wanted the Bleaks and a peace with the Druj. The flooded Vendarri sought a new home, possibly in Holberg. The Great Forest Orcs wanted the Heart of Peytaht retaken. The Montanian heretics claimed Hope's Rest. The Black Wind refused all talks. The Druj still held Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht. Dawn would not accept the Barrens ceasing to be Dawnish, and Cathan Canae's stance on ceding land complicated any concessions.

n.Dawn: Dawn held the Barrens and embraced Ser Dindrane's call to work with the orcs rather than flood the territory with settlers. Its people wanted the Towers of the Dawn rebuilt, the Fangs and Eaves of Peytaht made Dawnish bourse seats, and Dawnguard, Murderdale, the Carmine Fields and the Plains of Teeth kept, and would be outraged by any outcome that left the Barrens no longer Dawnish.
n.Druj: The Druj still held Murderdale and the Heart of Peytaht and were using them to launch attacks into the Barrens. Their expected return and reprisals against collaborators shaped the fears of every sept.
n.Highguard: Highborn priests used peerless kinship to mediate for Dawn, drawing on the Vendarri's surrender to them and their past work with the Great Forest Orcs. A proposed mandate would have Highguard help the Great Forest Orcs retake Peytaht instead of supporting an Imperial nation that season.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun had helped the Rahvin free themselves at the Fangs and some Imperial Orcs still supplied them. A relief mandate could make the Imperial Orcs the Empire's chosen negotiators with that sept.
n.Navarr: The Great Forest Orcs and Montanians had lived as guests of the Navarr in Therunin. Navarr mandates were offered to help the orcs retake the Heart of Peytaht; if the Highborn did so instead, most of the orcs would leave Therunin and the closeness with the Navarr would fade.
n.The League: The Vendarri asked for the Morass or Rebeshof in Holberg as a new home. The Sand Fishers objected strongly, warning that such a settlement would sour their relations with the League.
n.Urizen: Two alternative Urizeni mandates were offered: one urging the Citadel Guard to attack the Heart of Peytaht, the other calling on Urizeni to aid the Great Forest Orcs, as the Druj had been driven from Zenith.
n.Varushka: From Varushkan-held Ossium, the Menrothat offered a dose of black lotus in return for Farweald, and the Vendarri refused the Drownbark Forest because the Menrothat lived there.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: Astolat was expected to celebrate the Barrens being assigned to Dawn.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Great Forest Orcs had worked with the Highborn in Brocéliande, and Druj holdings in the Barrens could theoretically reach it.
t.Forest of Ulnak: Mentioned in passing: Rahvin slaves might be held there, the Dawnish wanted to campaign against it, and its Druj made Ossium unsafe for the Vendarri.
t.Holberg: The Vendarri asked for the Morass or Rebeshof, with an escort into Holberg, but the Sand Fishers warned against sharing the territory with them.
t.Ossium: The Menrothat of Ossium offered black lotus for Farweald, and Highborn priests suggested the Drownbark Forest to the Vendarri, who declined because of the Menrothat and the nearby Druj.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of the horrors the Druj inflicted when driven out.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: Mentioned in passing: more Rahvin slaves were believed held there, the Empire was striking against it, and the Dawnish wanted it invaded to secure the border.
t.Sarangrave: Mentioned in passing: it bordered the Karass regions, and the Dawnish wanted it invaded to push the Druj border beyond the Barrens.
t.Semmerholm: Mentioned in passing: expected to celebrate Dawn's gain of the Barrens, and theoretically within reach of Druj attacks from the Barrens.
t.The Barrens: Newly assigned to Dawn, the territory's septs each demanded regions of their own while the Druj still held two regions and no armies were present. The Wind set out options ranging from treaties and cessions to military action against the septs.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orcs and Montanians had lived in Therunin, though many Montanians were returning to Hope's Rest. A Highborn-led retaking of Peytaht would see most of the orcs leave Therunin.
t.Weirwater: Mentioned in passing: Weirwater was expected to celebrate the Barrens being assigned to Dawn.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a Urizeni mandate cited the Druj being driven from Zenith as inspiration to aid the Great Forest Orcs.

r.Brocéliande/Elerael: Mentioned in passing: Highborn and Great Forest Orcs had cooperated in Elerael over a shared interest in healing and herbs.
r.Brocéliande/Terunael: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs had been called to fight the Heirs of Terunael in Brocéliande.
r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Druj almost destroyed the Great Pits of Ennerlund, cited as proof of their spite.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: The Sand Fishers of Misericorde sent a delegation to Misericorde Market to protest against the Vendarri settling in Holberg.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: Rebeshof was the Vendarri's second choice of a new home if the Morass was unavailable.
r.Holberg/The Morass: The Morass was the Vendarri's preferred new home. The Senate could cede it, with an escort paid for by the treasury or provided by an Imperial army.
r.Ossium/Drownbark Forest: Highborn priests proposed the Drownbark marshes for the Vendarri, who rejected them because the Menrothat lived there and the Druj of Ulnak were nearby.
r.The Barrens/Bitter Strand: Around 750 Rahvin held the Fangs mithril mine here, and Bitter Strand was their first demand. The options set out ranged from recognising their control of the mine to besieging or attacking them.
r.The Barrens/Dawnguard: Returning Dawnish were reclaiming estates here and wanted the Towers of the Dawn rebuilt, while small Black Wind settlements remained in the region.
r.The Barrens/Farweald: The Menrothat of Ossium asked for Farweald in exchange for a dose of black lotus, a return opposed by every faction except the Karass.
r.The Barrens/Heart of Peytaht: The Druj still held the region and its weirwood grove, where Great Forest Orc slaves were at risk of massacre. Mandates and army orders were offered to retake it for the orcs.
r.The Barrens/Hope's Rest: Montanians were gathering at the ruins of Dourfell Keep and wanted Hope's Rest ceded to them. A single army could instead annihilate them there.
r.The Barrens/Murderdale: Murderdale remained under Druj control. The Rahvin wanted it ceded, the Dawnish regarded it as theirs, and the Great Forest Orcs would help claim it.
r.The Barrens/Saltmarsh: The Vendarri's home was wrecked by Imperial-raised floods. Conclave endowments, an Order mission, or an army protecting them could help, or the region could be ceded to them.
r.The Barrens/The Bleaks: The Karass withdrew into the Bleaks and wanted it ceded to them first; an Imperial army could attack them there at the Autumn Equinox.
r.The Barrens/The Plains of Teeth: The Karass abandoned most of their settlements here but asked for the region and the Towers of Dusk, which the Dawnish refused to give up.
r.The Barrens/The Untrod Groves: The Karass were digging in within the Untrod Groves, and a second army would be needed here to break them.

Raise Autumn Hammers.d: Proposed by the senator for Skarsind and seconded by The Barrens, the motion raised a legion from the Ethengraw sept, named the Autumn Hammers in deference to their heritage. It cost 200 wains of mithril and 75 thrones and would normally take a year. Bloodcrow Rasp and Irontide Flax supplied most of the mithril and thrones across Autumn 385YE and Winter 385YE, with Kostjya adding a single crown. Once fully funded, and thanks to Hammers of Fury, the army finished raising early, in time for its first general to be elected at the Spring Equinox 386YE. Because it was raised early it initially had no army quality and could take only standard army orders.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained their third army, the Autumn Hammers, funded largely by Bloodcrow Rasp and Irontide Flax, with its first general to be elected at the Spring Equinox 386YE.

t.Skarsind: The Autumn Hammers were raised in Skarsind from the Ethengraw sept, on a motion proposed by Skarsind's own senator.

Reconstruct the Tower of the Fall.d: Proposed by the senator for Zenith and seconded by Kahraman, the motion took up an existing opportunity arising from the Write your own ending wind of fortune. The rebuilt Tower of the Fall forms part of the Proffered Hand network and yields ten mana and six measures of heart's blood each season to the Keeper of the Tower of the Fall, an existing tenured Urizen title appointed by the Urizen senators. Herminius supplied the six wains of mithril and 9 thrones 6 crowns after the Autumn Equinox. The work, which took three months, is complete, and the Keeper's position becomes available for appointment again at the Winter Solstice 385YE.

n.Urizen: Urizen regained a working mana sinecure whose Keeper, a tenured Urizen title chosen by the nation's senators, receives ten mana and six heart's blood each season, with appointment possible again from Winter Solstice 385YE.

t.Zenith: Zenith gained a restored magical site linked to the Proffered Hand network, rebuilt at the urging of its own senator, who proposed the motion.

r.Zenith/Occursion: The Tower of the Fall in Occursion was rebuilt with mithril and money from Herminius of the Temple of the Wanderer and now produces mana and heart's blood each season.

Resonance and mitigation.d: Æsa Sigeling called for investigation into mitigating the detrimental effects of Imperial enchantments, while Ariadne of Auric Horizon committed the Conclave to completing the omnihedron. Urizen stargazers hold that the benefits outweigh the costs, but other nations doubt this, and many fear the next ritual will align the Empire with Winter. Cold Sun's heralds have killed hundreds, and the magistrates intend to investigate possible treason. The Conclave could still pass an Endorsement to protect those involved. The Marchers are enraged and are quietly considering withholding taxes. Attention now falls on the Witness of Conclave, the Imperial Censor, the Warmage, the Warcaster, the Imperial Magus and the Archmage of Day.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's armies are noted as being deeply engaged against the Druj while heralds roam Imperial territories.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the peace treaty with the Grendel is noted as being about to end, adding to the military pressure.
n.Highguard: Highborn magicians question rituals that draw inhuman forces' attention and keep opening regio, making a Vigilant watch almost impossible. Cold Sun's heralds now occupy Bastion.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's armies are noted as being deeply engaged against the Jotun.
n.Navarr: Navarr vates watching for Terunael-like hubris have voiced serious concerns about the Conclave's motives and cautioned against such tumultuous seasonal rituals. Heralds now threaten Hercynia and Miaren.
n.The Brass Coast: The Imperial Censor, Cassandra i Periera i Erigo of the Brass Coast, is singled out as able to interdict the practice of Imperial enchantments. Heralds are also present in Segura.
n.Urizen: Urizen's stargazers champion the omnihedron and believe its benefits outweigh its costs, while the enchantment is widely believed to have been raised by an Urizen coven. Bryn Netherwatch of Urizen, the Witness of Conclave, is under close scrutiny.
n.Varushka: Many Varushkan magicians broadly agree with the stargazers, having suffered only minimal ill effects from Imperial enchantments, though heralds of Cold Sun now roam Volodmartz and Karov.
n.Wintermark: Armies of Cold Sun's heralds are now present in the Wintermark territories of Kallavesa and Hahnmark.

t.Bastion: Bastion is one of eight territories where armies of murderous heralds of Cold Sun are now present.
t.Hahnmark: Armies of Cold Sun's warlike heralds are now at large in Hahnmark, killing anyone they encounter.
t.Hercynia: Hercynia is among the eight territories where Cold Sun's herald armies are now present.
t.Kallavesa: Cold Sun's herald armies are now present in Kallavesa, posing a magical military threat there.
t.Karov: Karov is one of the territories now hosting armies of Cold Sun's heralds.
t.Miaren: Armies of Cold Sun's heralds are now present in Miaren, destroying what offends them.
t.Segura: Segura is among the eight territories where Cold Sun's herald armies are now at large.
t.Volodmartz: Cold Sun's herald armies are now present in Volodmartz.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: Zenith is not named directly; the page refers only to Urizen's stargazers and an Urizen coven in general.

Restraint.d: Graciana proposed that the Senate hire mercenary patrols at ten thrones per territory each season, which would stop sweeping raids on personal resources but not attacks on commissions, named resources or armies. Alternatively, the Conclave could seek out whoever has been casting an unknown Autumn enchantment that protects Brass Coast territories, and have it added to Imperial Lore. Wintermark's Raven's Plight offered Gulnar's Eye as a reward for this. Freeborn families complained that the Conclave's deal letting Tharim feast on their mana sites and herb gardens amounted to raiding. They threatened to withhold taxes if such deals continued. Possible Synod mandates for the Brass Coast or Highguard assemblies would encourage tax refusal.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Graciana spoke with citizens who had endured years of Druj depredations.
n.Highguard: Jared of the Suns of Couros offered the Highborn Assembly a Partner of Greatness mandate supporting the Freeborn against the Tharim deal. If enacted, it would cut taxes from four Highborn territories through tax refusal.
n.Jotun: Recent Jotun raids into the western Empire informed the appraisal, which found that their organised warbands and armies could not be stopped by mercenary patrols alone. Tharim's knights are being provided to fight them.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Freeborn contrasted themselves with Navarr, saying they do not expect to sacrifice Prosperity to support an army.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn families resented Tharim draining their vervain and mana crystals under the Conclave's deal and warned they would withhold taxes over any future such agreements. Their territories had also been shielded by a mysterious protective enchantment.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Graciana spoke with Wintermark folk who had suffered Thule raids before the peace treaty.
n.Wintermark: The Steinr coven Raven's Plight offered Gulnar's Eye, a rare talisman boosting Autumn lore, to whoever shares the protective ritual so it can enter Imperial Lore. Graciana also drew on Wintermark's experience of Thule raids.

t.Bastion: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Bastion would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.
t.Casinea: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Casinea would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.
t.Hahnmark: The Raven's Plight, a Steinr coven based in Hahnmark, offered Gulnar's Eye, an artifact found in the Deeps, as a reward for bringing the anti-raiding enchantment into Imperial Lore.
t.Kahraman: If the proposed Brass Coast mandate were enacted, taxation from Kahraman would drop by about a tenth, rising to two fifths if unresolved by the Spring Equinox 386YE.
t.Madruga: If the proposed Brass Coast mandate were enacted, taxation from Madruga would drop by about a tenth, rising to two fifths if unresolved by the Spring Equinox 386YE.
t.Necropolis: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Necropolis would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.
t.Reikos: If the proposed Highborn mandate were enacted, taxation from Reikos would fall by about a tenth, rising further if the dispute went unresolved.
t.Segura: If the proposed Brass Coast mandate were enacted, taxation from Segura would drop by about a tenth, rising to two fifths if unresolved by the Spring Equinox 386YE.

Rimbaud eyes.d: Many League citizens moved to Spiral seeking opportunity, but election law barred nearly half of the newcomers from voting for the territory's first senator. Odhrin van Apulian, an ally of Kaliact, stood for the seat, while most orcs in Apulus stayed on the sidelines ahead of expected war with the Grendel. Kaliact suffered under a ruinous Urizen curse that threatened her fortune. Because the Urizen would not share the secret of the Block, commissions in Spiral needed extra mithril and cost 75 rings per wain. The Apulians chose to call audacity Pride and fidelity Loyalty, kept cunning private, and replaced retribution with dead reckoning. Not one newcomer founded a congregation.

n.Grendel: The Apulians were Grendel only three months earlier, war with the Grendel was expected, and orcs who opposed Kaliact stayed loyal to the Council of Salt Lords while many others in Apulus hedged their bets.
n.The League: The League took in the Apulians as new citizens, saw a rush of its people into Spiral chasing wealth and power, and faced a contested election for Spiral's senator. Its bishops and priests set up businesses there rather than congregations, while Apulian ideas of audacity and fidelity began spreading through the nation as Pride and Loyalty.
n.Urizen: A Urizen curse was ruining Kaliact's fortune, and the Apulians asked whether this cleared any reckoning the League owed Urizen. The Urizen still refused to share the secret of the Block, which pushed up building costs in Spiral, and they kept many congregations there.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: several citizens with Holberg names appear on the Spiral voter list, and Holberg-named priests put forward Synod judgements about the Apulians.
t.Spiral: Spiral faced its first senatorial election with a restricted electorate. A housing shortage and the need for mithril protection against the Black Plateau raised commission costs to 75 rings per wain, with extra mithril worth a fifth of the wain cost.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: citizens moving to Spiral from Tassato were exempt from the rule barring recent voters from the Spiral election.

r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus was flooded with League settlers short of protected housing, and its orc majority mostly held back from choosing sides between the League and the Salt Lords. No League congregation was established there, so League citizens in Apulus received no liao.

Schools and sawmills.d: The civil service tallied Sarvos 157, Holberg 153, Temeschwar 142, Tassato 35 and Apulian 2; the contest ends at the start of the Winter Solstice 385YE. Inspired by Holberg's popular sword academy, similar schools could be built in Sarvos, Tassato, Temeschwar or Apulus. Diora University proposed a College of the Arts in Cigno, which must be commissioned by the Winter Solstice. Veterans Lynada and Batheka proposed a Five Cities Military Academy in Tassato, allowing a third League army. The Sand Fishers finished their sawmills early and want a port at Misericorde, needing the Lakesedge Highway first. The Company of the Torch is terrorising Polseg in Vardstein Vale.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: a quoted statement of principle observed that Dawn and Varushka were currently winning the Semmerlak trade.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel invasion of Sarvos and the battle at Solen's Doubt are recalled, and about a dozen former Grendel have settled in Tassato.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: donations from Highborn citizens helped resolve Diora University's past financial troubles.
n.The League: The League's cities raced to finish Fransesca's contest and were offered sword academies, a College of the Arts, a military academy that could support a third army appointed perhaps by public auction, and a highway towards a Sand Fisher port.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka is named alongside Dawn as winning the Semmerlak trade, and the Varushkans' role at the Black Plateau is recalled in a veterans' argument.

t.Holberg: Holberg's bravos flocked to the sword academy to study philosophy, the Sand Fishers completed their sawmills, and a highway was proposed to open the way for a joint port on the Semmerlak; Holberg stood second in the contest with 153.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos led the contest with 157 and was offered a grand Diora University College of the Arts, plus the chance to build its own sword academy.
t.Spiral: The city of Apulian scored only 2 in the contest, having joined the League after it began, but could gain a sword academy, and its wealth was credited with making a third League army possible.
t.Tassato: Tassato lagged badly at 35, but veterans debating at the Barossa School proposed a Five Cities Military Academy there, and a sword academy could also be built.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar scored 142 and could build a sword academy, while the Company of the Torch menaced a mining settlement and the Custodian of the Assayer's Guild was charged with dealing with them.

r.Holberg/Ennerlund: Mentioned in passing: the Sand Fishers noted that no suitable port site exists along the Nameless River in Ennerlund.
r.Holberg/Holmauer: Mentioned in passing: the proposed Lakesedge Highway would begin at the Holmauer Gate of Holberg.
r.Holberg/Misericorde: A large orc-run sawmill was completed here, and the Sand Fishers proposed a port at Misericorde with discounted docking for League ships, reached via their settlement of Lakesedge.
r.Holberg/Rebeshof: The Lakesedge Highway, a 30-wain white granite road raised above the marshes, could be commissioned here, with a Rebeshof Roadwarden to keep it safe and collect tolls.
r.Holberg/Utterlund: A Sand Fisher sawmill was completed in Utterlund's forests, though the region was judged unsuitable for a port.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Cigno is the proposed site of the Diora University College of the Arts, which would create the Dioran Muse and must be commissioned by the end of the Winter Solstice 385YE.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulus was offered the chance to build its own sword academy combining swordplay and philosophy.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: Batheka d'Apulian and other former Grendel have settled here, and Tassato Regario is one of two possible sites for the proposed Five Cities Military Academy.
r.Temeschwar/Vardstein Vale: The brutal, changed Company of the Torch has been terrorising the mining settlement of Polseg, demanding the riches taken from Lorenzo's Deep Pockets.

Shining like fire.d: Every Imperial mine produced two extra ingots and suffered no accidents. People recovered lost items, confessed secrets and saw flaws in themselves and their surroundings, and stalled investigations were solved. Merrow felt calm and sensed magic, while mana sites became easier to establish and upgrade. Mana sites near Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue yielded Vitrified Oculi, and fifteen sinecures could be enhanced with weltsilver using the Windgleam Geometries. As side effects, shrouds below magnitude 100 collapsed, art and passion-based great works lost half their votes and liao, and labour costs for new Imperial commissions rose by half. The magnitude of Imperial enchantments rose to 210. Three skirmishes were also offered.

n.Dawn: The Rose Towers drew significantly fewer pilgrims as Day dissonance dulled appreciation of art, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Autumn Equinox.
n.Druj: A Druj patrol from across the Arkad, with a herald of the Queen of the Forest, was carrying the Vate's Shelter, taken from the Grynbor, back towards Turan. The Advisor on the Vallorn was tasked with reclaiming it.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel-held Feroz lay outside the enchantment, so its resources gained none of the benefits.
n.Highguard: Mana sites in Casinea each produced a Vitrified Oculus thanks to a Legacy of Virtue there. The Day magic also aided efforts to root out the espionage ring in Necropolis.
n.Jotun: A Jotun warband of Raoljost, Ulvenwar and Skjaldir held the Grimnir's Glass, a Phial of the Sun taken over a century ago, and faced Imperial efforts to reclaim it in Tromsa. Jotun-held Liathaven gained none of the enchantment's benefits.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: the Windgleam Geometries used to enhance sinecures with weltsilver draw on a long-neglected theory by the Navarr magician Donnaya Windgleam.
n.The Brass Coast: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse and the Crimson Drummers of Madruga saw far fewer attendees as Day dissonance smothered passion, halving their Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.
n.The League: League mana sites near Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue each produced a Vitrified Oculus. However, the Blood Red Quays Art Gallery, the Bloody Great Theatre and Lorenzo's Great Game lost visitors, and Tassato's merchant princes were targeted by bandits in Upwold.
n.The Marches: The Drake's Dozen bandits preyed on travellers on Upwold's long roads, and a skirmish was opened against them. The giant miner phantasm seen in Mournwold was cited as the kind of illusion that could not be raised during the Equinox.
n.Urizen: Multiple Urizen covens working together performed Bright Eyes Gleam in the Depths, the enchantment behind both its boons and its dissonances.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, but its mediators were targeted by the Drake's Dozen. The Grimnir of Wittal Grove was asked to reclaim the lost Grimnir's Glass from the Jotun in return for a seasonal gift of herbs.

t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: Brocéliande was not Imperial at the end of the Summer Solstice, so mines and resources there gained nothing from the enchantment.
t.Casinea: As home to one of Lorenzo's Legacies of Virtue, Casinea's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus of Day magic.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz lay outside the enchantment, and is used as an example of where a merrow's home would not prevent personal effects felt elsewhere.
t.Hahnmark: Mana sites near Hahnmark's Legacy of Virtue each produced a Vitrified Oculus, while mediators from Hahnmark were among the travellers targeted by the Drake's Dozen.
t.Holberg: Holberg's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus from its Legacy of Virtue, a great work designed with help from Holberg's Wunderkind guild.
t.Kahraman: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse saw far fewer attendees at its feasts and performances, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.
t.Kallavesa: Elina of Redleaf's Hall, a descendant of the founders of Wittal Grove's Healing House, traced the lost Grimnir's Glass. Redleaf's Hall offered seasonal herbs if it is returned to the hosts of Sulkavaris.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: Jotun-held Liathaven was outside the enchantment, so its resources received none of the effects.
t.Madruga: The Crimson Drummers of Madruga drew significantly smaller crowds under the Day dissonance, halving their Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.
t.Morrow: Mentioned in passing: a reformed League gossip writer announced plans to move to Morrow and become a torchbearer.
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the giant miner phantasm recently seen in Mournwold is cited as the kind of large illusion that would fail during the Equinox.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: the Day magic aided efforts to root out the espionage ring in Necropolis.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: used as an example of a territory where a merrow might have spent the season and felt the enchantment's effects.
t.Sarangrave: Over five thousand Imperials explored the Sarangrave during the season. A skirmish under Druj miasma was opened to intercept the Druj carrying the Vate's Shelter.
t.Sarvos: Sarvos's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, but the Blood Red Quays Art Gallery lost audiences, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.
t.Spiral: Shrouds over Spiral made with Sung's help survived the collapse of other shrouds. Merrow could also face the influence of the Black Plateau with calm focus.
t.Tassato: Tassato's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, while its merchant princes were favoured targets of the Drake's Dozen bandits in Upwold.
t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar's mana sites each produced a Vitrified Oculus, but the Bloody Great Theatre saw a significant drop in audiences, halving its Synod votes and liao for the Equinox.
t.The Barrens: Imperial scholars theorised that adding the Barrens, the largest territory the Empire has ever encountered, raised the magnitude of Imperial enchantments to 210.
t.Tromsa: Some Wittal Grove grimnir joined the Empire's push into Tromsa. A skirmish was opened at the Grove of Einar to recover the Grimnir's Glass from a Jotun warband.
t.Upwold: The Drake's Dozen preyed on traders between Redston and Ashill, evading magistrates and Eastern Guard troops. The Bailiff of the Grand Market was tasked with dealing with them.

r.Kahraman/Braydon's Jasse: The Azure Chorus at Braydon's Jasse saw significantly fewer people at its feasts and performances as Day dissonance dampened passion.
r.Kallavesa/Wittal Grove: The Grimnir of Wittal Grove, Branwynn Helsbur, was charged with reclaiming the Grimnir's Glass, lost around 238YE, in return for seasonal herbs from Redleaf's Hall.
r.Sarangrave/Bendol: Mentioned in passing: the Vate's Shelter was claimed from the Heirs of Terunael in connection with a visit to the vallorn-infested region of Bendol.
r.Sarangrave/Nesustak Forest: The Sentinel Gate was to open to the Queen's Claim in Nesustak Forest, where a Druj patrol carrying the Vate's Shelter could be intercepted under the miasma.
r.Tassato/Enterio: Mentioned in passing: the opening story is set at a country house in Enterio, where two siblings unearth their grandmother's hidden second will.
r.Tromsa/Icewood: The Grove of Einar in Icewood was the site of a skirmish to reclaim the Grimnir's Glass from a Jotun warband.
r.Upwold/The Heath: Tom's Dale in The Heath was the site of a skirmish against the Drake's Dozen bandits troubling the long roads of Upwold.

Ship to wreck.d: The Council of Salt Lords showed no interest in extending the treaty. Backed by the Asavean Plenum, they massed navies and armies even though Salt Lord Kaliact's defection and the loss of Spiral had disrupted their plans. Jarmish support for the Grendel ended thanks to Prospero. After the Equinox, every Imperial fleet in the Brass Coast, Highguard, Urizen, Feroz, Sarvos, Spiral and Tassato would lose a rank of production to Grendel raiding. Corsairs and Highborn captains kept trade with Sumaah open despite the Asavean blockade, though the Commonwealth and Sumaah grumbled about the Pact amendments. The Thule bought food with anonymous Imperial funds. The Faraden raised mithril prices after concessions to the Jotun. A Skouran delegation was expected at Anvil.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: Cedric Gallows of Dawn is named as Ambassador to the Iron Confederacy, and Jarrigk Orzel of Dawn as the Imperial Consul whom the Skourans wished to meet.
n.Grendel: With the treaty ending, the Salt Lords were set to return to war with Asavean backing. Independent Grendel pirates, privateers and followers of Siakha were expected to raid Imperial shipping with impunity for at least a season, though Kaliact's defection had forced them to rethink their strategy in the Bay.
n.Highguard: Highborn fleets were among those facing a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding. Highborn ship captains helped the corsairs break the Asavean blockade so that Sumaah trade could continue, and Accalon of Highguard served as Ambassador to the Sumaah Republic.
n.Jotun: The Jotun forced the Faraden to pay heavily for passage through the Lasambrian Hills. They also won concessions, including mithril and white granite sold to the orcs significantly cheaper than to Imperial traders.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Fintan Founder's Dance of Navarr is listed as Ambassador to Axos.
n.The League: League fleets in Sarvos, Spiral and Tassato faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding. League citizens held the posts of Ambassador to the Commonwealth and Ambassador to Faraden.
n.Thule: The Thule's food shortages eased markedly after an anonymous sum of Imperial money reached Rak Who-Speaks-For-The-Dragon's-Undivided. His agents used it to buy food in Imperial markets and ship it north.
n.Urizen: Urizeni fleets were among those facing a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding. Abel of Urizen was named Ambassador to the Grendel and Ariadne of the Auric Horizon Ambassador to Jarm.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Eska Crowspeaker of Wintermark is named as Voice of Liberty, and the quoted Liberty Pact amendment was raised by the senator for Sermersuaq.

t.Bay of Catazar: The Grendel still sought to rule uncontested over the Bay, and their raiders were set to prey on Imperial ships there. Jarmish vessels were reportedly leaving the Bay, while Axou traders grew reluctant to risk its sea-lanes.
t.Feroz: Governor Rahab still controlled Feroz, where corsairs had lost homes and boatyards. Fleets in Feroz faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding.
t.Necropolis: Mentioned in passing: intelligence captured in Necropolis revealed that recent losses had disrupted the Salt Lords' plans.
t.Otkodov: Reports from Otkodov described a marked improvement in its food crisis, as Imperial funds were used to buy food and ship it north to feed starving people.
t.Sarvos: Imperial fleets in Sarvos faced a one-rank production penalty following the Autumn Equinox as Grendel raiders attacked their ships.
t.Spiral: The Grendel's loss of Spiral had disrupted the Salt Lords' plans. Imperial fleets there now faced a one-rank production penalty from Grendel raiding.
t.Tassato: Imperial fleets in Tassato faced a one-rank production penalty following the Autumn Equinox as Grendel raiders attacked their ships.

Ten travellers tales.d: The Kabani traders returned to sell narcotics outside the Forge, though no Blue Lotus. Brewton merchants planned to sell their Bittersweet Brew at the same time. The Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende septs, whose armoury, ossuary and gardens the Imperial Orcs had built, came to pledge to the nation. The Axou scholar Theodosia landed at Crown's Quay holding the shield Bawn-watch. The Venturesome Harrier explorers returned from Screed's Black Plateau. Two Thule warlocks asked to meet Navarr scholars of the vallorn. The Jotun ghodi Osgar Hildsson sought talks on ancestors at the Tree of Names. Tassatan orcs came to watch their senator's election. Doktor Meier wished to debate the Greater Good. Pilgrims who had renounced Asavea landed near Sanctuary bearing news for Eli of the Cenotaph.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the three septs left Ossium after the Druj were defeated, having lived under them for years, and the Yerende's herbal arts are said to nearly rival those of the Druj.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Crown's Quay harbourmaster had uneasy dreams of Grendel invaders reaching the docks.
n.Highguard: Highguard's Necropolis shores received the Axou scholar Theodosia with the shield Bawn-watch at Crown's Quay. A Highborn Inquisitor confirmed the anointings of the Asavean pilgrims, and Highborn wayfarers then escorted them towards Anvil.
n.Imperial Orcs: Now that the Ethengraw Armoury, Illarawm Ossuary and Yerende Gardens are built, the three septs came to Anvil to formally pledge themselves to the nation and stand as equals beside the Sunstorm and Sannite septs.
n.Jotun: The Jotun ghodi Osgar Hildsson travelled alone under a flag of truce. He swore he sought no fight and wished only to discuss ancestors, mysticism and shared ancient culture.
n.Navarr: Two Thule warlocks acting for some of the Dragons asked the Ambassador to Otkodov to introduce them to Navarr scholars versed in the vallorn. A Navarri was also named as the new opposite number of the Crown's Quay harbourmaster.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the Axou scholar Theodosia has leased a small house on the outskirts of Myfanwy's Rest for her year-long stay in the Empire.
n.The League: Leaguers could expect the Harrier explorers' tale of Screed and their bid for investment, a Tassatan playwright seeking a dramaturgical company, and Tassatan orc business owners weighing up the senatorial candidates. The Harlequin had also invited the Kabani traders to a play premiere at the League Theatre.
n.Thule: Two prestigious Thule warlocks travelled from Otkodov on the personal business of two Dragons rather than the Five-Who-Are-One. They were escorted by blue-cloaked orc warriors.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: unlike earlier Thule delegations, the two warlocks expressed no interest in speaking to the people of Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Osgar Hildsson invited Wintermark mystics, and anyone interested, to meet him at the Tree of Names in the Wintermark camp to talk about ancestors and shared culture.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the orcs leaving Spiral mostly settled in Sarvos and Tassato, preferring not to stray too far from the Bay of Catazar.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the Brewton traders were making their way east to Casinea and Anvil.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: a few adventurous orc citizens from Spiral moved to Holberg.
t.Madruga: The visiting Axou scholar Theodosia has taken a lease on a small house on the outskirts of Myfanwy's Rest and is open to missives from Imperial scholars.
t.Necropolis: Theodosia landed at Crown's Quay with reams of paperwork and the shield Bawn-watch, declared as diplomatic luggage. Pilgrims who had renounced Asavea came ashore near the funerary jetties of Sanctuary and were questioned before being allowed onward.
t.Ossium: Mentioned in passing: the Ethengraw, Illarawm and Yerende septs left Ossium after the Druj were defeated.
t.Otkodov: Two Thule warlocks set out from Otkodov for Anvil in a covered ox wagon and asked the Ambassador to Otkodov for an introduction to Navarr vallorn scholars.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the harbourmaster thought of Reikos on recognising the Shield of Vigilance and wished it could stay.
t.Sarvos: Many of the new orc citizens leaving Spiral settled in Sarvos, and some of them established businesses there.
t.Skallahn: The Jotun ghodi Osgar Hildsson emerged from Skallahn under a flag of truce, bound for Anvil.
t.Skarsind: Skarsind has been home to the three septs since they arrived two years ago, and the Imperial Orcs have now built them an armoury, an ossuary and gardens.
t.Spiral: Some new orc citizens left Spiral for other League cities while human Leaguers moved in to become citizens of Apulian. Explorers also returned from an expedition to Screed.
t.Tassato: Tassatan orc business owners planned to watch their city's senatorial election and might back a candidate with their wealth. The explorer Alexandre and the playwright Mirabil also hail from Tassato.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: a few adventurous orc citizens from Spiral moved to Temeschwar.

r.Necropolis/Fishguard: Mentioned in passing: the harbourmaster sent Theodosia on her way to Fishguard after she landed.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named directly; the page describes arrivals on the Necropolis coast at Crown's Quay and near Sanctuary.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Mentioned in passing: Ossuary is not named directly; Spiral appears as the place many new orc citizens left and many human Leaguers moved to.
r.Spiral/Screed: The Company of the Venturesome Harrier claim to have climbed the south face of the Black Plateau in Screed with paying customers, and now seek investment for further expeditions.

The cities and the city.d: The Seventh Wave and Isaac of the Silent Tide broke the Grendel spy ring in Necropolis, ending Grendel trade with Highborn merchants. Seized papers showed the Salt Lords undecided on a target and keen to despoil the tombs by holding Coursmouth. The Shuttered Lantern, helped by the Wolves of War, mapped a separate ring in Sarvos that either could now destroy, and confirmed rings in Madruga, Redoubt, Tassato and Spiral. The Winter Sun's Day enchantment drew items of worth from the Highborn. Stewards found nothing amiss at Varkula's tomb. Building began in Bastion while some three thousand Cold Sun heralds gathered at Woodbury.

n.Druj: Their heartland of the Salt Flats of Sanath is under Imperial attack, and Imperial assemblies may urge their soldiers to reach out to orc septs oppressed by the Druj.
n.Grendel: Their Necropolis spy ring was rolled up and its agents expelled, their Sarvos network was mapped, and recovered papers exposed turmoil among the Salt Lords, their Asavean pact and their designs on the tombs of Necropolis.
n.Highguard: The Seventh Wave broke the Necropolis spy ring at the cost of Grendel trade, Highborn gave up items of worth to the Imperial Orcs, Highguard funds the Grand Inspiration in Bastion, and the Valiant Pegasus fights in Sanath while Cold Sun threatens the White City.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Winter Sun recovered items of worth from the Highborn in Necropolis and sent many to Skarsind's Halls of Worth, and Skywise Gralka's art was chosen as an inspiration for the sacred city in Bastion.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn are committing white granite and money to the Grand Inspiration until Summer 386YE, corsairs acting for a Madrugan magistrate exposed a Grendel smuggling ring, and a Grendel spy ring was confirmed in Madruga.
n.The League: A Grendel spy ring of mostly League citizens and disguised Salt Lord agents was mapped in Sarvos, which the Grendel may still attack. The Wolves of War could destroy the ring, and further rings were confirmed in Tassato and Spiral.
n.Urizen: Naris in Redoubt was named as one of two regions the Grendel must hold to strike Necropolis, a spy ring was confirmed in Redoubt, and the Urizen assembly may urge the Citadel Guard to seek out oppressed septs in Sanath.
n.Varushka: Wise ones sent under Father Drakov's statement were refused entry to Empress Varkula's tomb, which showed no sign of a rising sovereign, and the Varushkan assembly may direct the Iron Helms to seek out oppressed septs in Sanath.

t.Bastion: Construction of the Grand Inspiration of the Way began on the designs of Millward Cowley and Skywise Gralka, but a large Cold Sun force in the territory leaves workers, granite caravans and the unfortified White City vulnerable.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Bay of Catazar is not named on the page and relates only to the wider Grendel threat to the Empire's southern coast.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: a Grendel espionage ring was confirmed here, and corsairs acting for a Madrugan magistrate helped expose the Necropolis smuggling ring.
t.Necropolis: The Grendel spy ring and a smuggling ring were broken, ending extra Grendel trade, and the Winter Sun sought items of worth here. Seized papers showed the Grendel intend to despoil the tombs, while Varkula's tomb stayed sealed.
t.Redoubt: A Grendel spy ring was confirmed in Redoubt, and Naris was identified as one of two regions the Grendel must take to raid the Necropolis.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: Cold Sun had already destroyed the Unbound Steel Hall of Lost Chapters here.
t.Salt Flats of Sanath: The Valiant Pegasus and other Imperial armies are advancing into this Druj heartland. Assemblies may pass mandates trading slower conquest for contact with local septs, but these fail if any army makes a merciless assault.
t.Sarvos: A separate Grendel espionage ring was mapped in the city, which remains a possible Grendel target. The Shuttered Lantern, the Wolves of War or both could destroy the ring, and if left alone it could covertly aid an attack.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: many items of worth recovered in Necropolis are sent to Skarsind's Halls of Worth for the oathwrights to assign to new champions.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the Wolves of War's general boasted of taking Spiral in a single season, and a Grendel spy ring was confirmed here.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: listed among the territories where a Grendel espionage ring was confirmed.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's body was moved from Necropolis and interred in a new tomb here.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Winter Sun marched south from the Barrens, and the Dawnish approach used in its conquest is the model for the Sanath mandates.

r.Bastion/Stoneside: Cold Sun would need to pass through Stoneside to threaten the White City directly.
r.Bastion/Woodbury: Some three thousand Cold Sun heralds have gathered here, leaving its lightly fortified farming chapters terrified of losing their harvests and treasures if forced to flee.
r.Necropolis/Coursmouth: Grendel papers show they would need to occupy Coursmouth to break into the tombs of the Thrones and heroes, though a counterattack might trap such an army there.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: Mentioned in passing: Longbeach is not named on the page and relates only to the wider espionage and Grendel threat to Necropolis.
r.Redoubt/Naris: Naris is one of two regions the Grendel must take and hold to reach and raid the Necropolis.
r.Sarvos/Bocche: The Shuttered Lantern mapped Grendel agents here as part of a ring best struck in all three Sarvos regions at once.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: Grendel agents here form part of the Sarvos spy web, which needs simultaneous action in all three regions to dismantle.
r.Sarvos/Uccelini: Agents in Uccelini were mapped as part of the Sarvos ring, and if left in place they could covertly support a Grendel attack.

To the last syllable.d: Raids began during the Summer Solstice and grew more organised afterwards. Warnings from the Navarr, Dawnish and Vigilance assemblies saved many lives, but around two thousand citizens were slain. Freya's Garden, the Grand Conservatory of Music and the Hall of Lost Chapters were destroyed, and Therunin's trods were damaged. Every Imperial fortification lost 500 casualties and receives no resupply, except those in Dawn and Spiral and the Broch. Dawn, protected by Summer magic, lost no one. Cold Sun armies now stand in Rundhal Marsh, Valasmark, Northpines, Oakways, Livardz, Duzekani, Burnish and Woodbury. Enmity would cut off reinforcements but would not remove them. Sentinel Gate skirmishes are offered against further attacks.

n.Dawn: Under Meraud's Summer magic, Dawn's defenders were reinforced by heralds of Summer eternals and not a single Dawnish citizen was slain. Its fortifications were spared casualties, and the General of the Eastern Sky is summoned to defend Karov's Eternal Shafts of Time.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Druj are recalled as having once besieged the Great Library and as the horror the people of Zenith have already endured.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Brass Coast's loss of Feroz to the Grendel is cited as one reason for Freeborn fury.
n.Highguard: The Highborn assembly's warning failed to reach a greater majority, but congregations heeding Vigilance turned back an attack at Sybella. The Hall of Lost Chapters at Tabernacle was still destroyed, a Cold Sun army now holds ground in Woodbury, and Bastion's senator must defend the White Tower.
n.Imperial Orcs: The orc garrison of the Will fought several days of pitched battle to drive heralds from a Day regio in Estermark. The Halls of Worth now face a threat that falls to the Weigher of Worth, Ghillihg.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: recent Jotun invasions of Bregasland and of the Brass Coast's western territories are recalled.
n.Navarr: Navarr thorns heeded their assembly and fought Cold Sun across the Empire via the trods. However, the heralds have learned to burn out trods, damaging Therunin's network and threatening Hercynia's, and Cold Sun armies stand in Northpines and Oakways.
n.The Brass Coast: Families, hakima and kohan met every incursion with overwhelming fury born of past losses. A Cold Sun army is spreading across Burnish, and the Cerevado Nets are threatened.
n.The League: League cities quickly dealt with the heralds, the largest attack falling on Holberg. Spiral alone of all Imperial territories saw no heralds at all.
n.The Marches: The well-organised Marches drove off the heralds. Orcs and humans died defending Honour's Rest in the Mournwold, and the Keeper of the Dour Fens must stop heralds claiming the Still Rock in Bregasland.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: Miechernya is noted as a now Thule-controlled region beyond the Wulfric's Fall pass.
n.Urizen: All three Urizeni territories were attacked. Morrow and Zenith repelled the heralds with Day-realm and magical aid, but Redoubt's Grand Conservatory of Music was destroyed, and the Churn and the Brilliant Star are now threatened.
n.Varushka: Varushkan vales defeated the heralds with ruthless pragmatism, aided by patrols on the Iron Roads and Jaheris's servants at the Icy Crag. Cold Sun armies now stand in Livardz and Duzekani, and Veresk is in danger.
n.Wintermark: Hahnmark's beacons were lit too late to save Freya's Garden, though Kallavesa's beacons foiled the largest attack. Cold Sun armies now hold ground in Rundhal Marsh and Valasmark.

t.Astolat: The Prime Harp was targeted at the Solstice, but afterwards Meraud's golden lions fought beside Astolat's defenders while the Golden Sun celebrated there on furlough.
t.Bastion: An attack on Sybela and its Physician's Hall was intercepted with only token damage. A Cold Sun army has since appeared in Woodbury and is pushing towards the White Tower.
t.Bregasland: Still recovering from the Jotun invasion, Bregasland's beaters and its magical wards held off the heralds. A force is now moving to claim the Still Rock regio in Gravenmarch.
t.Brocéliande: Mentioned in passing: its Broch is exempt from the fortification losses because it lies outside Imperial territory.
t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: its loss to the Grendel is cited as fuelling Freeborn anger.
t.Hahnmark: Heralds destroyed Freya's Garden before the halls could rally. A Cold Sun army now stands in Valasmark, and the White Owl Hall in Kronemark is threatened.
t.Hercynia: A Cold Sun army is present in Northpines and is moving to burn out Hercynia's trods. If it succeeds, repairs will require a conjunction to Deer's Folly.
t.Holberg: The Pavilion on Looking Glass Lake was attacked at the Solstice, and Holberg suffered the largest League attack, which was dealt with by its fortification and watch.
t.Kahraman: A Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae helped the Freeborn defend the labour camps building roads and kamkrag, so no serious damage was done.
t.Kallavesa: After the Raven Seers of Ishal were attacked, a Suaq hero helped light the beacons in time to foil a second attack against Ishal. A Cold Sun army now holds ground in Rundhal Marsh.
t.Karov: A Cold Sun army stands in Duzekani, and heralds are marching on the Eternal Shafts of Time in Wieliczka.
t.Karsk: The weary defenders of Veresk face three bands of heralds and will fall unless the Empire intercepts one of them.
t.Madruga: Freeborn families crushed the heralds so swiftly that the armies stationed in Madruga barely had time to respond.
t.Miaren: The Pool of Silver Clouds was attacked at the Solstice, and a Cold Sun army now stands in Oakways.
t.Miekarova: The assault on the Icy Crag of the Eternal Sun became a siege, broken by the college's battle-magicians, the Gremani family and Jaheris's elfin warlocks before Grimhold's defenders arrived.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: Mitwold's only serious trouble came from other heralds, a matter left for another time.
t.Morrow: A crystal ward and the prismatic lizard-sentinels of the Celestial Library destroyed the heralds at Canterspire. Heralds now threaten the Churn geyser in Peregro.
t.Mournwold: Orcs and Marchers, with the beaters and the garrison of Farstrider's Watch, stopped a major attack on Honour's Rest, though many defenders died.
t.Redoubt: The Grand Conservatory of Music was destroyed, and the Tower of Light and Shadow was attacked at the Solstice. The Brilliant Star mine in Tomari is now threatened.
t.Reikos: The Grey Watch Grasses were attacked at the Solstice, and the Hall of Lost Chapters at Tabernacle was destroyed, with the town badly damaged.
t.Sarvos: The Wellspring of Jade was attacked at the Solstice. Like other League cities, Sarvos dealt quickly with the heralds.
t.Segura: A Cold Sun army is slowly spreading across Burnish, and heralds are advancing on the Cerevado Nets in Lucksprings.
t.Semmerholm: Not named individually, but as Dawnish land it shared in the Summer-aided defence in which no Dawnish citizen died.
t.Skarsind: Orc defenders fought for days to dislodge heralds fortifying a Day regio in Estermark. Heralds are now climbing towards the Halls of Worth in Gildermark.
t.Spiral: Alone of all Imperial territories, Spiral reported no heralds, and its two fortifications were spared casualties.
t.Tassato: The Blood Red River Museum was attacked during the Solstice, though League cities dealt quickly with the heralds.
t.The Barrens: Jaheris sent giant spiders, warlocks and goblin slingers from the ruins of the Towers of the Dawn to help households protect the new settlers.
t.The Semmerlak: Rhianos sent trident-wielding tritons to fight Cold Sun's heralds on the shores of the Semmerlak.
t.Therunin: Navarr and the Holt of the Oak saved Peakedge Stead, but its trods were damaged. They will slowly deteriorate unless repaired at a vallorn-quality regio.
t.Volodmartz: A Cold Sun army of around three thousand has appeared in Livardz.
t.Weirwater: The resting Eastern Sky went mana hunting here, and trumpets at Spiral Castle summoned its general to Karov.
t.Zenith: Defended by the Dripping Echoes ward, koboldi and heralds of Estavus, Zenith's furious sentinels drove the heralds into the marshes and forests of Lustri, and they did not return.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: An attack on Sybela was intercepted, and heralds are now moving to fortify the ruined White Tower, which would add a thousand strength to Cold Sun's push to claim the region.
r.Bastion/Woodbury: A Cold Sun army of around three thousand has coalesced in Woodbury.
r.Bregasland/Gravenmarch: Heralds are marching on the Still Rock, a potent unaligned Day regio. Holding it would let Cold Sun bring in another army even under enmity.
r.Hahnmark/Bruckland: If the White Owl Hall falls, citizens would begin withdrawing from Bruckland towards Kalpaheim.
r.Hahnmark/Kronemark: Heralds are advancing on the White Owl Hall of the Augurs of the Opalescent Gloaming, and the Imperial Seer is charged with stopping them.
r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Valasmark.
r.Hercynia/Deer's Folly: A conjunction to Deer's Folly would be needed to repair Hercynia's trods if the heralds burn them out.
r.Hercynia/Northpines: A Cold Sun army is present, and heralds who killed most of the Long Day striding are heading for a crossing of the trods.
r.Kallavesa/Rundhal Marsh: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Rundhal Marsh.
r.Karov/Duzekani: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Duzekani.
r.Karov/Wieliczka: Heralds are advancing on the Eternal Shafts of Time to slaughter the miners and seize their mithril.
r.Karsk/Nitrost: The vale of Veresk faces three bands of heralds, and a Sentinel Gate opens to Gulgisaz to intercept one of them.
r.Miaren/Oakways: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Oakways.
r.Miekarova/Miechernya: Mentioned in passing: named as the Thule-controlled region reached through the Wulfric's Fall pass.
r.Morrow/Peregro: Heralds are advancing on the Churn, a volatile geyser whose eruption would damage the Churnspire and the surrounding land.
r.Redoubt/Tomari: Heralds drawn by its Day affinity threaten the Brilliant Star mine, its workers and its mithril.
r.Reikos/Riverwatch: Mentioned in passing: not named on the page, and linked only through the attacks on Reikos.
r.Segura/Burnish: A Cold Sun army is slowly spreading across Burnish.
r.Segura/Lucksprings: Heralds are marching on the Cerevado Nets to slaughter the workers and claim the gathered ilium.
r.Skarsind/Estermark: Heralds fortified a hidden Day regio near Wulfric's Fall until the Will's garrison drove them back after days of battle; a watch now guards the regio.
r.Skarsind/Gildermark: Heralds are climbing towards the Halls of Worth above Gildenheim, threatening every orc trapped there.
r.Volodmartz/Livardz: A major Cold Sun army is now present in Livardz.
r.Zenith/Lustri: The defeated heralds were driven into the forests of Lustri and did not return.
r.Zenith/Proceris: Nightbound Proceris anchors the Dripping Echoes of the Fen ward that protected Zenith's defenders.

Various storms and saints.d: The Unfettered Mind found that Sadogua powers Dripping Echoes of the Fen and Irra Harah powers Forge the Wooden Fastness. Sadogua moved Damakhan's Forge from Spiral to Zenith in return for amity. Ephisis' Scales was suspended for the Equinox, Estavus barred Varushkan magicians from Before the Throne of Estavus for a year, and Basileus Flint was reportedly deposed. The Great Grasses blight kept slowly spreading. Kaela offered a compromise on extending her Gift to vallorn fighters. Janon's heralds inspired the Green Shield and Summer Storm and offered to transform the Burning Falcon. Sentinel Gate openings led to Southmoor and Sarvos, and a Varushkan expedition lost eight people at Zoria's Cave.

n.Dawn: The heralds of Barien chose to be hosted by House Griffinsong in Dawn, a reward for the Dawnish gift of power to the Summer eternals against the realm of Day.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: Kaela's Gift is described as letting Imperial citizens captured by the Druj escape torment through painless death.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Damakhan's Forge is described as battered by successive Grendel invasions, and Grendel-held Feroz is named in the Freeborn mandate.
n.Imperial Orcs: Janon's heralds will fight alongside the Summer Storm until Spring 386YE, inspiring Imperial Orc units that support it, though the army cannot use Give Ground or Cautious Advance.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's move into Tromsa and its conquest of Jotun lands is the campaign in which Janon's heralds aided two Imperial armies.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: Barien's heralds dropped their plan to enjoy Navarr hospitality, and the Spider King's watch over Navarr armies is used as a comparison.
n.The Brass Coast: Janon offered to give the Burning Falcon True Conviction if priests gather 50 wains of mithril and the National Assembly enacts a mandate before the Spring Equinox, while the hakima kept watch on the slowly spreading Great Grasses blight.
n.The League: Sanvar Isk opened the Loom of Spells in Tassato and will auction its use, while Lictors arrived in Sarvos to collect dramaturgical debts that could threaten League dramaturgy.
n.The Marches: Sadogua left an offer for Marcher landskeepers with the Marcher egregore, and threshers acting on Brother Martin Orchard's mandate tracked the Whisper Gallery cultist Quiet Charlie to Southmoor.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: a Thule raiding party is said to have looted Zoria's Cave over a century ago, probably taking the Staff of Zoria.
n.Urizen: The ruins of Damakhan's Forge now stand beside the Crucible of Fate in Zenith, and observers noted a new bitterness among Urizen magicians.
n.Varushka: Estavus barred Varushkan magicians from Before the Throne of Estavus until Autumn 386YE over an alleged theft, and a Varushkan expedition to Zoria's Cave lost eight people to a devouring darkness.
n.Wintermark: Zakalwe invited Winterfolk competitors to his strategy game, and Wintermark units supporting the Green Shield will be inspired by Janon's heralds for the coming year.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Feroz is named in the proposed Freeborn mandate as one of the territories from which everburning flames would be brought.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Kahraman is named in the proposed Freeborn mandate as one of the territories from which everburning flames would be brought.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: Madruga is named in the proposed Freeborn mandate as one of the territories from which everburning flames would be brought.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: the Maze of Zoria in Miekarova is noted as the site the Synod chose over Zoria's Cave for consecration.
t.Mournwold: The cultist Quiet Charlie was found meeting heralds near a Night chamber in Southmoor, and a Mournwold landskeeper reported a tulpa tempting him while working a green iron mine.
t.Ossium: The Unfettered Mind's findings should allow the Conclave to begin negotiating with the relevant eternals for a permanent fortification in Ossium, if it wishes.
t.Sarvos: Lictors beating sinister drums appeared at Bertram's Square to demand payment of debts owed by mountebanks who guised as dramaturgical personae.
t.Spiral: Sadogua removed the ruins of Damakhan's Forge from Spiral, leaving a crater already filling with water.
t.Tassato: An entrance to the Loom of Spells opened in Tassato, where many volunteers worked for Sanvar Isk in exchange for training in ritual theory.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Barrens is named as a place where Kaela's Gift is used by captured citizens, and the Bound King has shown interest in a regio there.
t.Tromsa: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's advance into Tromsa is where the Green Shield and Summer Storm first called on Janon's heralds.
t.Volodmartz: A Varushkan expedition to Zoria's Cave in Volodmartz's mountains found it consumed by a light-eating darkness, and eight members vanished.
t.Zenith: The ruins of Damakhan's Forge were set down less than half a mile from the Crucible of Fate, and the Urizen named the old site's crater Damakhan's Lake.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: Mentioned in passing: no events take place in Gambit; the word appears only in the name of Zakalwe's herald, the Opening Gambit.
r.Mournwold/Southmoor: The Sentinel Gate was set to open to Crowned Trees in Southmoor, where Brother Martin Orchard was to confront Quiet Charlie and gathered cultists and heralds.
r.Sarvos/Cigno: The Sentinel Gate was set to open to Bertram's Square in Cigno, allowing up to 50 people to settle the Lictors' dramaturgical debts.
r.Tassato/Tassato Mestra: An Autumn regio in Tassato Mestra released heralds who built the Bridges and Chains doorway to the Loom of Spells.
